french-upper-volta.t: The French colony centred on the Mossi kingdoms, abolished in 1932 and recreated in 1947, which became independent in 1960 and is now Burkina Faso.
french-upper-volta.o: [[e:france|France]] had conquered the region in the 1890s, taking [[s:kingdom-of-ouagadougou|Ouagadougou]], capital of the Kingdom of Ouagadougou, in 1896. The lands were first ruled as part of [[s:french-sudan|French Sudan]], and in 1919 the colony of [[e:upper-volta|Upper Volta]] was created, with its capital at Ouagadougou and [[e:edouard-hesling|Edouard Hesling]] as its first governor.
french-upper-volta.r: The colony, part of [[s:french-west-africa|French West Africa]], was densely populated but poor. [[e:france|France]] ruled through the [[e:mossi|Mossi]] kings, including the [[e:mogho-naba|Mogho Naba]], and used the colony as a reservoir of labour for railways and for plantations in the [[s:french-ivory-coast|French Ivory Coast]]. In 1932 it was abolished and divided among the [[e:ivory-coast|Ivory Coast]], [[s:french-sudan|French Sudan]] and the [[s:colony-of-niger|Colony of Niger]], partly to supply labour.
french-upper-volta.e: [[e:mossi|Mossi]] chiefs and politicians lobbied for its restoration, achieved in 1947. [[e:upper-volta|Upper Volta]] became an autonomous republic in 1958 and independent on 5 August 1960 under [[e:maurice-yameogo|Maurice Yameogo]]. It was renamed [[e:burkina-faso|Burkina Faso]] in 1984.

free-imperial-city-of-frankfurt.t: Main river trading city where German kings were elected and later crowned, famous for its fairs, its Jewish quarter and as birthplace of Goethe.
free-imperial-city-of-frankfurt.o: [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]] grew around a Carolingian palace at a ford over the Main. Royal assemblies met there, and its fairs grew into some of the most important in [[e:europe|Europe]]. The citizens gained self-government in the 13th century, and from about 1245 it was treated as an imperial city.
free-imperial-city-of-frankfurt.r: A patrician council ruled. The [[e:golden-bull-of-1356|Golden Bull of 1356]] made [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]] the place of royal elections, and from 1562 coronations also took place in its cathedral. Its autumn fair and book fair drew merchants from across [[e:europe|Europe]]. [[e:jews|Jews]] lived in the walled [[e:frankfurt-judengasse|Judengasse]], attacked in the [[e:fettmilch-uprising|Fettmilch Uprising]] of 1614. The city turned Lutheran, and [[e:johann-wolfgang-von-goethe|Goethe]] was born there in 1749.
free-imperial-city-of-frankfurt.e: In 1806 [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]] lost its freedom to [[e:karl-theodor-von-dalberg|Dalberg]], becoming capital of the [[s:grand-duchy-of-frankfurt|Grand Duchy of Frankfurt]]. In 1815 it became a free city, seat of the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]] and of the 1848 [[e:frankfurt-parliament|Frankfurt Parliament]]. [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] annexed it in 1866.

free-and-independent-state-of-cundinamar.t: A centralist republic around Bogotá that fought rival federalists during Colombia's 'Foolish Fatherland' before the Spanish reconquest.
free-and-independent-state-of-cundinamar.o: After the [[e:bogota|Bogotá]] revolution of 20 July 1810, the province of Santa Fe proclaimed the State of Cundinamarca. Its constitution of 1811, under President [[e:jorge-tadeo-lozano|Jorge Tadeo Lozano]], still recognised [[e:ferdinand-vii-of-spain|Ferdinand VII]] as king. [[e:antonio-narino|Antonio Nariño]], who had translated the Rights of Man in 1794, soon took power and favoured a strong central government.
free-and-independent-state-of-cundinamar.r: Cundinamarca refused to join the federalist [[s:united-provinces-of-new-granada|United Provinces of New Granada]], and the two sides fought a civil war in 1812 and 1813. [[e:antonio-narino|Nariño]] repelled a federalist attack on [[e:bogota|Bogotá]] in January 1813, and in July Cundinamarca declared full independence from [[e:spain|Spain]]. Nariño then led a campaign against royalists in the south but was captured at [[e:pasto|Pasto]] in 1814.
free-and-independent-state-of-cundinamar.e: In December 1814 [[e:simon-bolivar|Simón Bolívar]], serving the [[s:dutch-republic|United Provinces]], captured [[e:bogota|Bogotá]] and forced Cundinamarca to join the federation. [[e:pablo-morillo|Pablo Morillo's]] royalist army retook Bogotá in 1816, ending the first period of independence.

free-imperial-city-of-gelnhausen.t: Town on the Kinzig founded by Frederick Barbarossa, whose imperial palace hosted the 1180 diet that stripped Henry the Lion of his duchies.
free-imperial-city-of-gelnhausen.o: [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Emperor Frederick Barbarossa]] founded Gelnhausen in 1170 as a market town, granting it privileges and building an imperial palace on an island in the [[e:kinzig-main|Kinzig]] river. It lay on the trade road from [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]] to [[e:leipzig|Leipzig]]. In 1180 the palace hosted the [[e:imperial-diet|imperial diet]] that issued the [[e:gelnhausen-charter|Gelnhausen Charter]], dividing the lands of [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]].
free-imperial-city-of-gelnhausen.r: As an imperial city Gelnhausen was governed by a council of [[e:burghers|burghers]] under the emperor's protection, prospering from trade along the road between [[e:frankfurt|Frankfurt]] and the east. Its [[e:marienkirche-gelnhausen|Marienkirche]], with an unusual eastern tower group, and the ruined palace are among the finest [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]] buildings. The town was too small to defend its autonomy for long once Hohenstaufen power collapsed.
free-imperial-city-of-gelnhausen.e: In 1349 King Charles IV pledged the city to the [[e:house-of-schwarzburg|Counts of Schwarzburg]], and the pledge later passed to the Counts of [[s:county-of-hanau-munzenberg|Hanau]] and the [[s:electoral-palatinate|Electoral Palatinate]], which ruled it jointly. It kept a nominal imperial status until 1803, when it went to [[s:electorate-of-hesse|Hesse-Kassel]]. It is now a town in [[e:hesse|Hesse]].

free-imperial-city-of-schweinfurt.t: Imperial city on the Main destroyed in the margrave war of 1554 and birthplace of the Leopoldina, Germany's oldest academy of sciences.
free-imperial-city-of-schweinfurt.o: Schweinfurt grew around a crossing of the Main and was rebuilt after destruction in the 13th century, being recognised as an imperial city around 1254. It lay between the lands of the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[e:wurzburg|Würzburg]] and the [[e:house-of-hohenzollern|Hohenzollerns]] and had to defend its freedom against both.
free-imperial-city-of-schweinfurt.r: A council of [[e:burghers|burghers]] ruled, and the town lived from trade on the Main, crafts and wine. It adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in 1542. In the [[e:second-margrave-war|Second Margrave War]] Margrave [[e:albert-alcibiades-margrave-of-brandenburg-kulmbach|Albert Alcibiades]] of [[s:principality-of-brandenburg-bayreuth|Brandenburg-Kulmbach]] occupied it, and in 1554 his enemies destroyed the city. In 1652 four Schweinfurt physicians founded the academy later known as the [[e:leopoldina|Leopoldina]].
free-imperial-city-of-schweinfurt.e: Schweinfurt lost its freedom in 1802 when [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] annexed it. In the 19th century it became an industrial town known for ball bearings, and it is now in Bavaria. The [[e:leopoldina|Leopoldina]] is [[e:germany|Germany's]] national academy of sciences.

french-guiana.t: France's territory on the South American mainland, once a notorious penal colony and today home to Europe's spaceport at Kourou.
french-guiana.o: French attempts to settle [[e:cayenne|Cayenne]] began in the early 17th century, including one in 1643 that ended in disaster. In 1664 a lasting settlement was established at Cayenne under [[e:antoine-lefebvre-de-la-barre|Antoine Lefebvre de La Barre]]. The [[e:dutch|Dutch]] and English contested it, but [[e:france|France]] held it from 1676, apart from a Portuguese-Brazilian occupation from 1809 to 1817.
french-guiana.r: The colony produced [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]], [[e:spice-trade|spices]] and annatto with enslaved African labour, but the population remained small. The [[e:kourou-expedition|Kourou expedition]] of 1763 sent some 12,000 settlers, most of whom died of disease. [[e:slavery|Slavery]] was abolished in 1794, restored in 1802 and finally ended in 1848. From 1852 to 1953 the colony held a penal colony, the bagne, including the [[e:iles-du-salut|Îles du Salut]], where [[e:alfred-dreyfus|Alfred Dreyfus]] was held on [[e:devils-island|Devil's Island]]. Gold rushes drew prospectors from the 1850s.
french-guiana.e: French Guiana became an overseas [[e:departement|department]] of [[e:france|France]] in 1946. The [[e:guiana-space-centre|Guiana Space Centre]] opened at [[e:kourou|Kourou]] in 1968 and now launches European [[e:ariane-rocket-family|Ariane]] rockets. Since 2015 it has been a single territorial collectivity, part of the [[e:european-union|European Union]].

free-imperial-city-of-kempten.t: Protestant imperial city that stood beside the Catholic Prince-Abbey of Kempten, two rival states sharing one town until 1803.
free-imperial-city-of-kempten.o: The town of [[e:kempten|Kempten]] grew beside the [[s:prince-abbey-of-kempten|Prince-Abbey of Kempten]], which originally held lordship over it. The [[e:burghers|burghers]] gained growing autonomy, and in 1289 [[e:rudolf-i-of-germany|King Rudolf I]] granted them the rights of an imperial city. Disputes with the abbey continued for centuries.
free-imperial-city-of-kempten.r: A council of [[e:guild|guilds]] and patricians governed the small walled town, which lived from crafts, linen and trade on the [[e:iller|Iller]]. In 1525, in the so-called Great Purchase, the town bought out the abbot's remaining rights over it. It adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]], becoming a Lutheran island beside the Catholic abbey town. Both towns were damaged in [[e:thirty-tyrants|the Thirty]] Years War.
free-imperial-city-of-kempten.e: [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] annexed the imperial city in 1802 and the abbey in 1803, and in 1818 the two were united into one town. [[e:kempten|Kempten]] is now a Bavarian city, and its old imperial town and abbey quarter remain distinct.

first-philippine-republic.t: Constitutional republic proclaimed at Malolos in 1899, often called the first in Asia, which fought the United States for independence.
first-philippine-republic.o: Following the [[s:revolutionary-government-of-the-philippines|Revolutionary Government of the Philippines]] and the drafting of the [[e:malolos-constitution|Malolos Constitution]] by a congress of revolutionary delegates, the Philippine Republic was inaugurated at [[e:barasoain-church|Barasoain church]] in [[e:malolos|Malolos]] on 23 January 1899, with [[e:emilio-aguinaldo|Emilio Aguinaldo]] as president and [[e:apolinario-mabini|Apolinario Mabini]] as head of the cabinet.
first-philippine-republic.r: The constitution established a parliamentary system with an assembly, separation of church and state, and civil rights. In practice the war with the [[s:united-states|United States]], which began on 4 February 1899, absorbed all efforts. The government moved from [[e:malolos|Malolos]] to [[e:san-fernando-pampanga|San Fernando]], [[e:tarlac-city|Tarlac]] and other towns as American forces advanced, and turned to [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrilla]] warfare in late 1899.
first-philippine-republic.e: [[e:emilio-aguinaldo|Aguinaldo]] was captured at [[e:palanan|Palanan]] in March 1901 and swore allegiance to the [[s:united-states|United States]]. Generals such as [[e:miguel-malvar|Miguel Malvar]] fought on until 1902. Though defeated, the republic became a foundation of Filipino national identity, and its flag and anthem were later adopted by the [[s:philippines|Philippines]].

cr.a: See File history below for details.

french-cochinchina.t: The southern third of Vietnam, ruled directly by France as a colony from the 1860s, with Saigon as its capital and rice and rubber as its wealth.
french-cochinchina.o: [[e:france|France]] attacked [[e:da-nang|Da Nang]] in 1858 and captured [[e:ho-chi-minh-city|Saigon]] in 1859. By the [[e:treaty-of-saigon-1862|Treaty of Saigon]] in 1862 [[e:tu-duc|Emperor Tu Duc]] of the [[s:nguyen-dynasty|Nguyen dynasty]] ceded three eastern provinces, and in 1867 Admiral [[e:pierre-paul-de-la-grandiere|de La Grandiere]] seized the three western ones, completing the colony of [[s:nguyen-lords|Cochinchina]].
french-cochinchina.r: Unlike the [[e:protectorate|protectorates]] of [[s:french-protectorate-of-annam|Annam]] and [[s:french-protectorate-of-tonkin|Tonkin]], [[s:nguyen-lords|Cochinchina]] was a full colony under French law, with an elected colonial council and a deputy in the French parliament. Canals and drainage opened the [[e:mekong-river|Mekong]] delta to [[e:rice|rice]] exports, and [[e:rubber|rubber]] plantations spread in the east. [[e:ho-chi-minh-city|Saigon]] and [[e:cholon|Cholon]] grew into a major port with large Chinese communities. Religious movements such as [[e:caodaism|Cao Dai]] and [[e:hoa-hao|Hoa Hao]] arose.
french-cochinchina.e: After the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]] [[e:france|France]] set up the [[s:autonomous-republic-of-cochinchina|Autonomous Republic of Cochinchina]] in 1946. In 1949 [[s:nguyen-lords|Cochinchina]] was merged into the [[s:state-of-vietnam|State of Vietnam]] under [[e:bao-dai|Bao Dai]], ending its separate status.

french-ionian-islands.t: Ionian Islands under French rule after the fall of Venice, twice annexed by France between 1797 and 1814 and finally held only at Corfu.
french-ionian-islands.o: [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] destruction of the [[s:republic-of-venice|Republic of Venice]] in 1797 brought French troops to [[s:corcyra|Corfu]]. The [[e:treaty-of-campo-formio|Treaty of Campo Formio]] in October 1797 gave [[e:france|France]] the [[s:venetian-ionian-islands|Venetian Ionian Islands]] and their mainland outposts, which were organised as three French [[e:departement|departments]]: [[e:corcyre-department|Corcyre]], [[e:ithaque-department|Ithaque]] and [[e:mer-egee|Mer-Egee]].
french-ionian-islands.r: The French burned the Golden Book of the Venetian nobility, planted liberty trees and introduced revolutionary institutions, but their requisitions and anticlericalism alienated many islanders. A Russian-Ottoman expedition under Admiral [[e:fyodor-ushakov|Ushakov]] took the islands in 1799, creating the [[s:septinsular-republic|Septinsular Republic]]. The [[e:treaties-of-tilsit|Treaty of Tilsit]] in 1807 returned them to [[e:france|France]].
french-ionian-islands.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] blockaded and captured most of the islands in 1809-1810, but the French governor General [[e:francois-xavier-donzelot|Donzelot]] held [[s:corcyra|Corfu]] until it was surrendered in 1814 after [[e:napoleon|Napoleon's]] abdication. The islands then became the [[s:united-states-of-the-ionian-islands|United States of the Ionian Islands]] under British protection.

free-imperial-city-of-wimpfen.t: A small imperial city on the Neckar, built beside the largest Hohenstaufen palace, that kept its freedom until 1803.
free-imperial-city-of-wimpfen.o: [[e:bad-wimpfen|Wimpfen]] stands on a hill above the [[e:neckar|Neckar]] near a Roman fort. Around 1200 the [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]] built their largest imperial palace there, and the town that grew beside it received town rights. After the fall of the Hohenstaufen, Wimpfen counted as a free imperial city by about 1300, while Wimpfen im Tal below kept its collegiate church of Saint Peter.
free-imperial-city-of-wimpfen.r: A council of [[e:burghers|burghers]] ran the city and its tiny territory, which lived from [[e:neckar|Neckar]] shipping, crafts and farming. The town adopted [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] in the 16th century, though the collegiate foundation in the valley stayed Catholic. In 1622 the [[e:battle-of-wimpfen|Battle of Wimpfen]] was fought nearby, a victory for [[e:johann-tserclaes-count-of-tilly|Tilly]]'s [[e:catholic-league|Catholic League]] army over Margrave [[e:george-frederick-margrave-of-baden-durlach|George Frederick]] of [[s:margraviate-of-baden-durlach|Baden-Durlach]].
free-imperial-city-of-wimpfen.e: In the mediatisation of 1802 and 1803 [[e:bad-wimpfen|Wimpfen]] passed briefly to [[e:baden|Baden]] and then to [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Hesse-Darmstadt]], remaining a Hessian exclave until after the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]]. Salt springs found in 1817 made it a spa, and as Bad Wimpfen it is now part of [[e:baden-wurttemberg|Baden-Württemberg]].

french-congo.t: France's colony north of the Congo River, founded through Brazza's treaties and notorious for its concession-company abuses.
french-congo.o: In 1880 [[e:pierre-savorgnan-de-brazza|Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza]] signed a treaty with the [[s:kingdom-of-tio|Makoko]], ruler of the Kingdom of Tio, placing land north of the [[e:congo-river|Congo River]] under French protection; [[e:brazzaville|Brazzaville]] grew from his post. The [[e:berlin-conference|Berlin Conference]] of 1884-1885 recognised French claims, and the territories were united with [[s:gabon-french-colony|Gabon]] as the colony of Gabon-Congo, renamed French Congo in 1891.
french-congo.r: [[e:pierre-savorgnan-de-brazza|Brazza]] was commissioner-general until 1897, ruling with few resources from [[e:libreville|Libreville]]. From 1899 the government handed most of the land to about forty concession companies, which forced Africans to collect [[e:rubber|rubber]] and [[e:ivory-trade|ivory]], leading to scandals and depopulation. A commission led by Brazza investigated the abuses in 1905.
french-congo.e: In 1903 the colony was divided into [[s:gabon-french-colony|Gabon]], [[s:middle-congo|Middle Congo]] and Ubangi-Shari-[[e:chad|Chad]], and in 1910 these were organised as [[s:french-equatorial-africa|French Equatorial Africa]], with [[e:brazzaville|Brazzaville]] as capital. The concession system left a lasting legacy of depopulation and distrust.

free-imperial-city-of-metz.t: A self-governing patrician republic in Lorraine, one of the richest cities of the Empire, which France seized and held against Charles V in 1552.
free-imperial-city-of-metz.o: The citizens of [[e:metz|Metz]] gradually took power from their [[e:bishop|bishops]] during the 12th century, and by the late 12th century the city governed itself under the emperor's protection, outside the [[s:prince-bishopric-of-metz|Prince-Bishopric of Metz]]. A master-échevin elected each year headed the city government from 1180.
free-imperial-city-of-metz.r: [[e:metz|Metz]] was run by the paraiges, a handful of patrician family associations that monopolised offices. Its merchants and bankers lent money to princes across the region, and the city controlled a sizable rural territory. Metz fought the dukes of [[s:duchy-of-lorraine|Lorraine]] and withstood a siege by [[e:charles-vii-of-france|Charles VII]] and [[e:rene-of-anjou|René of Anjou]] in 1444.
free-imperial-city-of-metz.e: In 1552 [[e:henry-ii-of-france|Henry II of France]] occupied [[e:metz|Metz]] under the [[e:treaty-of-chambord|Treaty of Chambord]] with German Protestant princes. [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]] besieged it in the winter of 1552–1553 but [[e:francis-duke-of-guise|Francis of Guise]] held it. Metz became French, which the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] confirmed in 1648.

free-state-of-thuringia.t: Union of seven small Thuringian states in 1920, which saw the first Nazi minister and later disappeared into East German districts.
free-state-of-thuringia.o: After 1918 the small Ernestine and [[s:county-of-schwarzburg|Schwarzburg]] states and Reuss sought union. On 1 May 1920 Saxe-Weimar-[[e:eisenach|Eisenach]], Saxe-[[e:meiningen|Meiningen]], Saxe-[[e:altenburg|Altenburg]], Saxe-[[e:gotha|Gotha]], [[s:principality-of-schwarzburg-rudolstadt|Schwarzburg-Rudolstadt]], [[s:principality-of-schwarzburg-sondershausen|Schwarzburg-Sondershausen]] and the [[s:peoples-state-of-reuss|People's State of Reuss]] merged into the Land of [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]], with [[e:weimar|Weimar]] as capital. [[e:coburg|Coburg]] chose [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] instead.
free-state-of-thuringia.r: [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]] had textile, toy, glass and optical industries, including [[e:carl-zeiss-ag|Carl Zeiss]] in [[e:jena|Jena]]. In 1923 a left-wing government was removed by the federal army. The [[e:bauhaus|Bauhaus]] left [[e:weimar|Weimar]] for [[e:dessau|Dessau]] in 1925 under nationalist pressure. In 1930 [[e:wilhelm-frick|Wilhelm Frick]] became Thuringia's interior minister, the first Nazi to hold a ministerial post. [[e:buchenwald-concentration-camp|Buchenwald concentration camp]] was built near Weimar in 1937.
free-state-of-thuringia.e: After 1945 [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]] was in the Soviet zone and became a Land of the [[e:east-germany|German Democratic Republic]]. In 1952 it was divided into the districts of [[e:erfurt|Erfurt]], Gera and [[e:suhl|Suhl]]; the state was re-established in 1990.

free-imperial-city-of-aachen.t: Charlemagne's favourite residence and the coronation city of German kings for six centuries, a free imperial city until the French annexed it.
free-imperial-city-of-aachen.o: [[e:charlemagne|Charlemagne]] built his palace and the [[e:palatine-chapel-aachen|Palatine Chapel]] at [[e:aachen|Aachen]], around hot springs, and was buried there in 814. Otto I was crowned in the chapel in 936, beginning a tradition of royal coronations. In 1166 [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]], having had Charlemagne canonised in 1165, granted the town a charter of liberties.
free-imperial-city-of-aachen.r: [[e:aachen|Aachen]] was governed by a council of patricians and [[e:guild|guild]] representatives. Some thirty German kings were crowned there until 1531. Its economy rested on cloth and brass making, as well as pilgrimage to relics shown every seven years. A great fire in 1656 destroyed much of the city, and later spas attracted European visitors.
free-imperial-city-of-aachen.e: The city hosted peace congresses in 1668 and 1748. French revolutionary troops occupied it in 1794, and it was formally annexed by [[e:france|France]] under the [[e:treaty-of-luneville|Treaty of Lunéville]] in 1801. In 1815 it became Prussian. [[e:aachen-cathedral|Aachen Cathedral]] was among the first [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Sites]].

firdafylke.t: Petty kingdom of the western Norwegian fjords of Sunnfjord and Nordfjord, one of the realms conquered by Harald Fairhair.
firdafylke.o: Firdafylke, the land of the fjord districts between [[s:sogn|Sogn]] and Møre, is known almost entirely from [[e:snorri-sturluson|Snorri Sturluson's]] sagas. It appears as one of the small coastal kingdoms of western [[e:norway|Norway]] in the century before unification.
firdafylke.r: Little is recorded beyond the sagas. Its people farmed the narrow fjord valleys and fished the coast, and like neighbouring fylki it had its own assembly. Many families from the district later took part in the settlement of [[s:republic-of-iceland|Iceland]].
firdafylke.e: According to [[e:heimskringla|Heimskringla]], its king Audbjørn fell fighting [[e:harald-fairhair|Harald Fairhair]] at the Battle of Solskjel, and the district then passed under Harald's earls. It became part of the [[s:kingdom-of-norway|Kingdom of Norway]] and of the [[e:gulating|Gulating]] law province.

free-imperial-city-of-buchau.t: One of the smallest free imperial cities, a town on the Federsee that shared its island site with a powerful abbey of noblewomen.
free-imperial-city-of-buchau.o: [[e:bad-buchau|Buchau]] grew on an island in the [[e:federsee|Federsee]] in upper [[e:swabia-bavaria|Swabia]] beside the abbey of noble canonesses founded there in the 8th century. The townspeople gradually freed themselves from the abbess's lordship, and by 1320 the town counted as a free imperial city answerable only to the emperor.
free-imperial-city-of-buchau.r: A council governed a town of a few hundred households with almost no territory, living from fishing, farming and crafts. Relations with the [[s:imperial-abbey-of-buchau|Imperial Abbey of Buchau]] next door produced constant lawsuits. The town remained Catholic and sat on the Swabian bench of cities. From the late 16th century it was home to a notable Jewish community.
free-imperial-city-of-buchau.e: In 1803 the town was mediatised and given, together with the abbey, to the princes of [[s:principality-of-thurn-and-taxis|Thurn und Taxis]]; in 1806 it passed to the [[s:kingdom-of-wurttemberg|Kingdom of Württemberg]]. Now [[e:bad-buchau|Bad Buchau]], it is a spa town known for the prehistoric lake settlements of the [[e:federsee|Federsee]] moor.

free-imperial-city-of-schwabisch-hall.t: Salt-producing imperial city on the Kocher that gave its name to the heller coin and became an early stronghold of the Reformation under Johannes Brenz.
free-imperial-city-of-schwabisch-hall.o: Hall grew around salt springs on the [[e:kocher|Kocher]], worked since Celtic times. Its mint produced the [[e:heller-coin|Haller pfennig]], or heller, from the 12th century. The town was a [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]] possession, and in 1280 [[e:rudolf-i-of-germany|King Rudolf I]] confirmed its independence from local lords, establishing it as an imperial city.
free-imperial-city-of-schwabisch-hall.r: Patrician families who owned shares in the salt works dominated the council until [[e:guild|guilds]] gained seats in the early 16th century. Salt boiling provided most of the city's wealth. Hall built a sizeable rural territory, buying [[s:lordship-of-limpurg|Limpurg]] castle in 1541. From 1522 the preacher [[e:johannes-brenz|Johannes Brenz]] led a moderate [[e:protestant-reformation|Lutheran Reformation]] that influenced much of south-western [[e:germany|Germany]].
free-imperial-city-of-schwabisch-hall.e: The city was annexed by Württemberg in 1802, and the salt works became a state enterprise. It is now a town in [[e:baden-wurttemberg|Baden-Württemberg]], its old town and the great steps of [[e:st-michaels-church-schwabisch-hall|St. Michael's Church]] well preserved.

free-imperial-city-of-windsheim.t: Small Franconian imperial city on the Aisch, surrounded by Hohenzollern lands, which adopted the Reformation and kept its freedom until 1802.
free-imperial-city-of-windsheim.o: [[e:bad-windsheim|Windsheim]] grew from a Frankish royal estate and later belonged to the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[e:wurzburg|Würzburg]] before returning to the Empire. It was recognised as an imperial city in the mid 13th century, around 1248, on the road between [[s:free-imperial-city-of-nuremberg|Nuremberg]] and Würzburg.
free-imperial-city-of-windsheim.r: The town was governed by a council and lived from farming, wine, crafts and its market. It was surrounded by the lands of the [[e:house-of-hohenzollern|Hohenzollern]] margraves of [[s:principality-of-brandenburg-ansbach|Ansbach]], on whom it depended for trade and with whom it often quarrelled. [[e:bad-windsheim|Windsheim]] adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in the 1520s and subscribed to the [[e:augsburg-confession|Augsburg Confession]] soon after it was presented in 1530.
free-imperial-city-of-windsheim.e: The city lost its freedom when it was annexed by [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] in 1802. Its saline springs later made it a spa, renamed [[e:bad-windsheim|Bad Windsheim]], and it now hosts the Franconian Open-Air Museum of rural buildings.

free-city-of-riga.t: The largest Hanseatic city of Livonia, which fought the Livonian Order and its archbishops for its liberties until it submitted to Poland in 1581.
free-city-of-riga.o: Riga was founded by [[e:albert-of-riga|Bishop Albert]] in 1201 and soon received its own town law. By the late 13th century its merchant council was strong enough to act independently, and it joined the [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanseatic League]] in 1282, controlling trade along the [[e:western-dvina|Daugava]] with [[e:polotsk|Polotsk]] and [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]].
free-city-of-riga.r: The city was governed by a council of merchants, with [[e:guild|guilds]] for merchants and craftsmen. Its rivalry with the [[s:livonian-order|Livonian Order]] led to open war from 1297; the city even allied with pagan [[s:grand-duchy-of-lithuania|Lithuania]], but the Order captured it in 1330. Riga exported [[e:fur-trade|furs]], wax, [[e:flax|flax]] and [[e:timber|timber]] and adopted [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] in 1522, one of the first cities outside [[e:germany|Germany]] to do so.
free-city-of-riga.e: When [[s:terra-mariana|Terra Mariana]] collapsed in 1561, Riga refused to submit and remained a free city for twenty years. In 1581 it accepted the rule of [[e:stephen-bathory|Stephen Báthory]] of Poland-[[e:lithuania|Lithuania]], and it later became the capital of [[s:swedish-livonia|Swedish Livonia]] and then of the [[s:governorate-of-livonia|Governorate of Livonia]].

faridkot-state.t: A Sikh princely state of the Malwa region of Punjab, ruled by Brar Jat Rajas from 1763 until 1948.
faridkot-state.o: [[e:hamir-singh-of-faridkot|Hamir Singh]], a [[e:brar-clan|Brar Jat]] chief, established himself at Faridkot around 1763, when [[e:sikhism|Sikh]] power spread across the plains after the [[e:durrani-empire|Durrani]] wars. The town took its name from the [[e:sufism|Sufi]] saint [[e:baba-farid|Baba Farid]].
faridkot-state.r: Faridkot came under British protection in 1809. Raja [[e:pahar-singh-of-faridkot|Pahar Singh]] sided with the British in the [[e:first-anglo-sikh-war|First Anglo-Sikh War]] in 1845 and was rewarded with land. The state had an 11-gun salute and a mostly [[e:sikhism|Sikh]] rural population; its rulers built schools, a hospital and the [[e:british-raj|Raj]] Mahal palace.
faridkot-state.e: [[e:harinder-singh-brar|Harinder Singh Brar]] acceded to [[e:india|India]] in 1947 and Faridkot was merged into the [[s:patiala-and-east-punjab-states-union|Patiala and East Punjab States Union]] in 1948. His death in 1989 was followed by a long legal dispute over the family estate.

free-imperial-city-of-dortmund.t: Westphalian imperial city on the Hellweg, a leading Hanseatic town that held off Cologne in the Great Feud of 1388 to 1389.
free-imperial-city-of-dortmund.o: Dortmund grew around a royal court on the [[e:hellweg|Hellweg]], the trade road between the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] and the [[e:weser|Weser]]. Ottonian kings held assemblies there, and by around 1220 it was the only imperial city in [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]]. Its merchants traded across the [[e:north-sea|North Sea]] and Baltic, and it became a leading member of the [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanseatic League]].
free-imperial-city-of-dortmund.r: A council of merchant patricians ruled the city. Its free court was the leading tribunal of the Vehmic courts of [[e:westphalia|Westphalia]]. In the [[e:great-dortmund-feud|Great Dortmund Feud]] of 1388 to 1389 it withstood a siege by the Archbishop of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-cologne|Cologne]] and the Count of the Mark. The city was surrounded by Mark territory and gradually lost trade. [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]] was introduced in the 1560s and 1570s.
free-imperial-city-of-dortmund.e: In 1803 Dortmund lost its freedom and was given to the house of [[s:principality-of-nassau-diez|Nassau-Orange]]. It belonged to the [[s:grand-duchy-of-berg|Grand Duchy of Berg]] from 1808 and to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] from 1815, growing into a great [[e:coal|coal]] and [[e:steel|steel]] city of the [[e:ruhr|Ruhr]].

federated-shan-states.t: The British union of more than thirty Shan and other hereditary states of eastern Burma, created in 1922 and governed from Taunggyi.
federated-shan-states.o: In 1922 the British combined the protected Shan states and the Wa states under a federal council, separating them from ministerial [[s:myanmar|Burma]] when the Dyarchy reforms gave the province partial self-government. The commissioner was based at [[e:taunggyi|Taunggyi]].
federated-shan-states.r: The saophas kept their hereditary positions and authority over local affairs, while a British commissioner controlled policing, finances and public works through a Federal Council of Chiefs. A common budget funded roads and schools. The federation remained separate from the parliamentary system set up in [[s:myanmar|Burma]] in 1937. Japanese and Thai forces occupied the area in the [[e:second-world-war|Second World War]].
federated-shan-states.e: At the [[e:panglong-conference|Panglong Conference]] of 1947 Shan leaders agreed with [[e:aung-san|Aung San]] to join an independent [[s:myanmar|Burma]], and the Federated [[e:shan-state|Shan States]] became Shan State of the Union of [[e:burma|Burma]] in 1948.

free-state-of-brunswick.t: Republican successor of the Duchy of Brunswick, remembered for giving Adolf Hitler German citizenship in 1932.
free-state-of-brunswick.o: [[e:ernest-augustus-duke-of-brunswick|Duke Ernest Augustus]] abdicated on 8 November 1918, and a socialist republic was proclaimed in [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]]. After a period of councils and unrest, a constitution was adopted in 1922, making Brunswick a parliamentary free state.
free-state-of-brunswick.r: [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]] had industry, canning and the [[e:bussing|Büssing]] vehicle works, and its politics were polarised between Social Democrats and the right. From 1930 the [[e:nazism|Nazis]] shared government, and in February 1932 the Nazi interior minister [[e:dietrich-klagges|Dietrich Klagges]] appointed [[e:adolf-hitler|Adolf Hitler]] to a nominal post in the state's [[e:berlin|Berlin]] legation, which made the stateless Hitler a German citizen and allowed him to run for president.
free-state-of-brunswick.e: After 1945 [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]] was in the British zone. In November 1946 it was merged with [[e:hanover|Hanover]], [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] and [[s:principality-of-schaumburg-lippe|Schaumburg-Lippe]] into the new state of [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]].

federation-of-south-arabia.t: Britain's last attempt to build a friendly state around Aden, which collapsed under nationalist insurgency in 1967.
federation-of-south-arabia.o: In April 1962 the [[s:federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south|Federation of Arab Emirates of the South]] was renamed the Federation of [[e:south-arabia|South Arabia]]. In January 1963 the [[s:colony-of-aden|Colony of Aden]] joined as the [[s:state-of-aden|State of Aden]], despite opposition from [[e:aden|Aden's]] trade unions and nationalists, and more [[e:protectorate|protectorate]] states joined in the following years.
federation-of-south-arabia.r: The federation was ruled by sultans, [[e:emir|emirs]] and sheikhs with British advisers, and [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] kept its military base at [[e:aden|Aden]]. In December 1963 a grenade attack on the High Commissioner at Aden airport led to a state of emergency. Two rival movements, the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] and [[e:front-for-the-liberation-of-occupied-south-yemen|FLOSY]], fought the British and each other in Aden and the Radfan mountains.
federation-of-south-arabia.e: In 1966 [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] announced it would leave without a defence agreement. In 1967 the federal army and states collapsed as the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] took over; [[e:britain|Britain]] withdrew on 29 November 1967 and [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]] became independent.

free-imperial-city-of-nordlingen.t: Walled Swabian imperial city inside the Ries meteorite crater, known for its Whitsun fair and the two battles of Nördlingen in the Thirty Years War.
free-imperial-city-of-nordlingen.o: A royal estate at Nördlingen in the [[e:nordlinger-ries|Ries]] basin, an ancient meteorite crater, passed to the [[e:bishop|bishop]] of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-regensburg|Regensburg]] and back to the [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]]. In 1215 [[e:frederick-ii|Emperor Frederick II]] recognised it as an imperial city, and its growth was helped by its position on the roads between [[e:franconia|Franconia]], Swabia and [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]].
free-imperial-city-of-nordlingen.r: A council dominated by merchants ruled the city. Its Whitsun fair was one of the leading markets of southern [[e:germany|Germany]], and cloth, leather and [[e:fur-trade|furs]] were its main trades. Nördlingen adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in the 1520s. The great hall church of [[e:st-georg-nordlingen|St. Georg]], with its tall tower known as the Daniel, and an intact ring of walls testify to its wealth.
free-imperial-city-of-nordlingen.e: The city suffered in [[e:thirty-tyrants|the Thirty]] Years War, when imperial and Spanish troops won the first [[e:battle-of-nordlingen-1634|Battle of Nördlingen]] in 1634 and French forces fought there again in 1645. It lost its freedom in 1803 to the [[s:electorate-of-bavaria|Electorate of Bavaria]].

former-yan.t: The Murong Xianbei kingdom that rose in Liaoning and briefly ruled the North China Plain from Ye, until the Former Qin conquered it in 370.
former-yan.o: The [[e:murong-xianbei|Murong Xianbei]] settled in western [[e:liaoning|Liaoning]] in the 3rd century and adopted farming and Chinese administration under [[e:murong-hui|Murong Hui]]. His son [[e:murong-huang|Murong Huang]] declared himself King of Yan in 337, moving the capital to [[e:chaoyang-liaoning|Longcheng]] (Chaoyang) in 342. He destroyed the [[s:yuwen-xianbei|Yuwen Xianbei]] in 344 and sacked the [[s:goguryeo|Goguryeo]] capital in 342.
former-yan.r: Former Yan combined [[s:xianbei|Xianbei]] cavalry with Chinese officials and farmers resettled from the war-torn plain. After [[s:later-zhao|Later Zhao]] collapsed, [[e:murong-jun|Murong Jun]] conquered the north-east plain, captured [[e:ran-min|Ran Min]] in 352, proclaimed himself emperor and moved the capital to Ye in 357. The regent [[e:murong-ke|Murong Ke]] was a capable administrator and general.
former-yan.e: After [[e:murong-ke|Murong Ke]] died, court jealousy drove out the talented general [[e:murong-chui|Murong Chui]], who had defeated [[e:huan-wen|Huan Wen]] at [[e:battle-of-fangtou|Fangtou]] in 369; he fled to [[s:former-qin|Former Qin]]. In 370 the [[e:qin-dynasty|Qin]] chancellor [[e:wang-meng-former-qin|Wang Meng]] took Ye and captured the emperor [[e:murong-wei|Murong Wei]]. [[e:murong-xianbei|Murong]] princes later founded [[s:later-yan|Later Yan]], [[s:western-yan|Western Yan]] and [[s:southern-yan|Southern Yan]].

free-imperial-city-of-gengenbach.t: A small Black Forest imperial city in the Kinzig valley that grew around a Benedictine abbey and kept its freedom until 1803.
free-imperial-city-of-gengenbach.o: Gengenbach grew around a Benedictine abbey founded in the 8th century. The town received its rights under the [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]] and in the 14th century became a free imperial city, recognised by Charles IV in 1360. With [[s:free-imperial-city-of-zell-am-harmersbach|Zell am Harmersbach]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-offenburg|Offenburg]] it lay within the imperial bailiwick of the [[e:ortenau|Ortenau]], which emperors often pledged to neighbouring princes.
free-imperial-city-of-gengenbach.r: A council of [[e:burghers|burghers]] governed the town, whose economy rested on wine, [[e:timber|timber]], crafts and traffic along the [[e:kinzig-rhine|Kinzig]] valley route through the [[e:black-forest|Black Forest]]. Relations with the abbey were often tense. Gengenbach briefly accepted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] but returned to [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]]. French troops burned it in 1689 during the [[e:nine-years-war|Nine Years' War]], and it was rebuilt in [[e:baroque|Baroque]] style.
free-imperial-city-of-gengenbach.e: In 1803 the mediatisation gave Gengenbach and its neighbours to [[e:baden|Baden]], which became the [[s:grand-duchy-of-baden|Grand Duchy of Baden]] in 1806. Its half-timbered old town, walls and town hall survive.

federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia.t: Present-day Ethiopia, a federation of ethnically defined regions and Africa's second most populous country, shaped by rapid growth and civil conflict.
federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia.o: The constitution adopted in December 1994 replaced the [[s:transitional-government-of-ethiopia|Transitional Government of Ethiopia]], and after elections the Federal Democratic Republic of [[e:ethiopia|Ethiopia]] was proclaimed in August 1995. [[e:meles-zenawi|Meles Zenawi]] of the [[e:ethiopian-peoples-revolutionary-democratic-front|EPRDF]] became prime minister, holding power until his death in 2012.
federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia.r: The constitution created a federation of ethnically based regional states, each with the right to self-determination. Under the [[e:ethiopian-peoples-revolutionary-democratic-front|EPRDF]] [[e:ethiopia|Ethiopia]] achieved rapid economic growth through state-led investment in roads, dams and industry, but the party dominated politics and suppressed opposition. A war with [[s:state-of-eritrea|Eritrea]] from 1998 to 2000 and the disputed elections of 2005 marked its early years.
federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia.e: Protests brought [[e:abiy-ahmed|Abiy Ahmed]] to power in 2018; he made peace with [[s:state-of-eritrea|Eritrea]] and won the [[e:nobel-peace-prize|Nobel Peace Prize]] in 2019. The [[s:tigray|Tigray]] war of 2020 to 2022, ended by the [[e:pretoria|Pretoria]] agreement, killed hundreds of thousands. [[e:ethiopia|Ethiopia]] remains a federal republic with [[e:addis-ababa|Addis Ababa]] as capital.

free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck.t: The Queen of the Hanse, a Baltic port whose law and merchants shaped dozens of towns from Tallinn to Gdańsk and which stayed a free state until 1937.
free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck.o: [[e:henry-the-lion|Henry the Lion]] refounded [[e:lubeck|Lübeck]] on the [[e:trave|Trave]] in 1159 as a German port to the Baltic. After his fall the town came under the emperor, and in 1226 Frederick II granted it the status of a free imperial city. Its merchants soon led the [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanseatic League]], which held its diets in Lübeck.
free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck.r: A council of merchant families ruled the city, and [[e:lubeck|Lübeck]] law was adopted by about a hundred Baltic towns. Wealth came from trade in herring, salt, grain, [[e:fur-trade|furs]] and [[e:timber|timber]], visible in the [[e:holstentor|Holstentor]] and [[e:st-marys-church-lubeck|St. Mary's Church]]. Lübeck turned Lutheran in 1530, and under the mayor [[e:jurgen-wullenwever|Jürgen Wullenwever]] it waged the disastrous [[e:counts-feud|Count's Feud]] against [[e:denmark|Denmark]] in 1534 to 1536.
free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck.e: As the [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanse]] faded [[e:lubeck|Lübeck]] declined. It was annexed by [[e:france|France]] from 1811 to 1813, then joined the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]] and [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] as a city-state. The [[e:greater-hamburg-act|Greater Hamburg Act]] of 1937 merged it into [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]]. Its old town is a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|World Heritage Site]].

free-state-of-bavaria.t: Bavaria as a republic, from the 1918 revolution through the Nazi era to a prosperous and self-confident state of modern Germany.
free-state-of-bavaria.o: On 7 November 1918 the [[e:independent-social-democratic-party-of-germany|Independent Socialist]] [[e:kurt-eisner|Kurt Eisner]] proclaimed the Free State of [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] in [[e:munich|Munich]], ending the Wittelsbach monarchy. Eisner was assassinated in February 1919, and a short-lived [[s:bavarian-soviet-republic|Bavarian Soviet Republic]] was crushed that spring. The [[e:bamberg|Bamberg]] constitution of 1919 established Bavaria as a parliamentary free state.
free-state-of-bavaria.r: Inter-war [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] became a conservative stronghold and refuge of the extreme right, where Hitler's [[e:beer-hall-putsch|Beer Hall Putsch]] failed in 1923. After 1933 the [[e:nazism|Nazis]] took control and [[e:munich|Munich]] became the capital of the movement. After 1945 Bavaria was in the American zone; its 1946 constitution created a state long dominated by the [[e:christian-social-union-in-bavaria|Christian Social Union]], which built a high-technology economy.
free-state-of-bavaria.e: [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] joined the [[s:federal-republic-of-germany|Federal Republic of Germany]] in 1949, though its Landtag rejected the [[e:basic-law-for-the-federal-republic-of-germany|Basic Law]] while accepting its validity. It remains one of [[e:germany|Germany's]] sixteen states, with [[e:munich|Munich]] as capital.

french-fourth-republic.t: France's post-war parliamentary republic, unstable in government but launching European integration and rapid economic growth before collapsing over Algeria.
french-fourth-republic.o: After the [[s:provisional-government-of-the-french-republic|Provisional Government of the French Republic]], voters approved a new constitution in October 1946. It created a strong [[e:national-assembly-of-france|National Assembly]] and a weak president; [[e:vincent-auriol|Vincent Auriol]] was the first. The colonies were reorganised as the [[e:french-union|French Union]].
french-fourth-republic.r: Coalitions changed constantly, with more than twenty governments in twelve years. Yet economic modernisation was rapid, guided by [[e:jean-monnet|Jean Monnet's]] planning. [[e:robert-schuman|Robert Schuman]] proposed the European [[e:coal|Coal]] and [[e:steel|Steel]] Community in 1950, and [[e:france|France]] signed the [[e:treaty-of-rome|Treaty of Rome]] in 1957. Defeat at [[e:battle-of-dien-bien-phu|Dien Bien Phu]] ended the [[e:indochina|Indochina]] war in 1954, and [[e:pierre-mendes-france|Pierre Mendès France]] negotiated the withdrawal.
french-fourth-republic.e: The Algerian War, begun in 1954, divided the nation. In May 1958 army officers and settlers seized power in [[e:algiers|Algiers]], and parliament called back [[e:charles-de-gaulle|Charles de Gaulle]], who drew up a new constitution creating the [[s:french-fifth-republic|French Fifth Republic]].

french-saint-barthelemy.t: Small, dry French island in the Leewards that passed through the hands of the Knights of Malta before France traded it to Sweden in 1784.
french-saint-barthelemy.o: French settlers from [[s:colony-of-saint-christopher|Saint Kitts]], sent by the governor [[e:phillippe-de-longvilliers-de-poincy|Philippe de Longvilliers de Poincy]], occupied [[s:saint-barthelemy-swedish|Saint-Barthélemy]] in 1648. In 1651 the island was included in the sale of French [[e:caribbean|Caribbean]] islands to the [[e:knights-hospitaller|Knights Hospitaller]]. A [[e:kalinago|Kalinago]] attack in 1656 wiped out the settlement, and it was repopulated only slowly, partly by settlers from [[s:duchy-of-normandy|Normandy]] and [[s:duchy-of-brittany|Brittany]].
french-saint-barthelemy.r: Lacking water and good soil, the island never became a plantation colony. Its small population of white smallholders lived by fishing, salt, livestock and modest [[e:cotton|cotton]] growing, with relatively few enslaved people. It was governed as a dependency of [[s:colony-of-guadeloupe|Guadeloupe]] or [[s:colony-of-saint-christopher|Saint Kitts]] rather than as a full colony, and its harbour, [[e:gustavia|Le Carénage]], was the only real settlement. The British occupied it briefly in the 18th century.
french-saint-barthelemy.e: In 1784 [[e:louis-xvi|Louis XVI]] ceded the island to [[e:sweden|Sweden]] in exchange for trading rights in [[e:gothenburg|Gothenburg]]. The Swedes renamed the harbour [[e:gustavia|Gustavia]] and made it a free port. [[e:france|France]] bought the island back in 1878, and it is now an overseas collectivity of France.

free-imperial-city-of-ulm.t: Danube imperial city of fustian weavers and merchants, builder of the minster with the world's tallest church spire and a leader of the Swabian League.
free-imperial-city-of-ulm.o: Ulm grew around a royal palace at the meeting of the [[e:blau-river|Blau]] and the [[e:danube|Danube]], recorded from 854. It was a favoured [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]] town, and after their fall it was confirmed as an imperial city, its privileges renewed by Rudolf I in 1274.
free-imperial-city-of-ulm.r: The [[e:schworbrief|Schwörbrief]] of 1397 gave the [[e:guild|guilds]] a majority on the council, and the mayor swore an annual oath to the citizens. Fustian weaving and the [[e:danube|Danube]] trade made Ulm rich, and it acquired the largest territory of any imperial city after [[s:free-imperial-city-of-nuremberg|Nuremberg]]. Its citizens began the minster in 1377. Ulm led the Swabian city leagues and the [[e:swabian-league|Swabian League]], and turned Protestant in 1530 to 1531.
free-imperial-city-of-ulm.e: Ulm lost its freedom to [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] in 1802 and passed to Württemberg in 1810; [[e:napoleon|Napoleon]] defeated an Austrian army there in 1805. The minster spire was completed in 1890, and [[e:albert-einstein|Albert Einstein]] was born in Ulm in 1879.

first-republic-of-armenia.t: The first modern Armenian state, born in 1918 amid war, genocide and famine, which survived two and a half years before Sovietisation.
first-republic-of-armenia.o: As the [[s:transcaucasian-democratic-federative-republic|Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic]] broke up, the Armenian National Council declared independence on 28 May 1918, just as Armenian forces halted an Ottoman offensive at [[e:battle-of-sardarabad|Sardarabad]]. The [[e:treaty-of-batum|Treaty of Batum]] in June 1918 left the new state a small territory around [[e:yerevan|Erivan]], crowded with refugees from the Armenian [[e:genocide|genocide]].
first-republic-of-armenia.r: The republic was governed by the [[e:armenian-revolutionary-federation|Armenian Revolutionary Federation]], with prime ministers [[e:hovhannes-kajaznuni|Hovhannes Kajaznuni]] and [[e:alexander-khatisian|Alexander Khatisian]] and a parliament elected by universal suffrage, including women. It faced famine, epidemics and border wars with [[s:georgia|Georgia]] and [[s:azerbaijan|Azerbaijan]]. After the Ottoman defeat it expanded to [[e:kars|Kars]], and the [[e:treaty-of-sevres|Treaty of Sevres]] in 1920 promised it much of eastern [[e:anatolia|Anatolia]].
first-republic-of-armenia.e: In autumn 1920 Turkish nationalist forces invaded, and in December 1920 the government ceded power to the [[e:communist-party-of-the-soviet-union|Bolsheviks]], creating the [[s:armenian-ssr|Armenian SSR]]. Its flag and anthem were revived by independent [[s:armenia|Armenia]] in 1990-1991.

first-maldivian-republic.t: A short-lived republic that briefly replaced the Maldivian sultanate in 1953 under Mohamed Amin Didi.
first-maldivian-republic.o: [[e:mohamed-amin-didi|Mohamed Amin Didi]], a reforming politician and prime minister, led the [[s:republic-of-maldives|Maldives]] towards abolishing the sultanate after the throne fell vacant. A referendum approved a republic, which was proclaimed on 1 January 1953, with Amin Didi as president, while the islands remained a British [[e:protectorate|protectorate]].
first-maldivian-republic.r: [[e:mohamed-amin-didi|Amin Didi]] pursued modernisation, promoting education, women's rights and the nationalisation of the fish export trade. These policies, together with food shortages and a ban on tobacco smoking, made his government unpopular.
first-maldivian-republic.e: While [[e:mohamed-amin-didi|Amin Didi]] was abroad for medical treatment in 1953 he was overthrown; he died early in 1954 after an attack by a crowd. The republic was abolished and the [[s:sultanate-of-the-maldives|Sultanate of the Maldives]] was restored in 1954.

fadhli-sultanate.t: A tribal sultanate on the Abyan coast east of Aden, a member of the British-backed south Arabian federation until 1967.
fadhli-sultanate.o: The Fadhli tribe held the coastal plain of Abyan and the hills behind it. In the late 17th century, as the [[s:qasimid-state|Qasimid State]] lost its hold over the south, the Fadhli chiefs established an independent sultanate, with [[e:shuqra|Shuqra]] on the coast as its chief town.
fadhli-sultanate.r: The sultans governed through tribal custom, controlling routes between [[e:aden|Aden]] and the interior. In the 19th century they often raided the outskirts of [[s:aden-settlement|British Aden]] before signing a protection treaty with [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]], becoming part of the [[s:aden-protectorate|Aden Protectorate]]. From the 1940s the Abyan irrigation scheme turned the delta into a [[e:cotton|cotton]]-growing area, bringing new revenue. The sultanate joined the [[s:federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south|Federation of Arab Emirates of the South]] in 1959.
fadhli-sultanate.e: It was a member of the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]] until 1967, when the [[e:national-liberation-front-south-yemen|National Liberation Front]] took over the territory, abolished the sultanate and incorporated it into [[s:south-yemen|South Yemen]].

fifteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.t: The Hyksos kings of Avaris, rulers of Levantine origin who governed northern Egypt for about a century.
fifteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.o: Around 1650 BCE rulers of Levantine descent, called [[e:hyksos|Hyksos]] from the Egyptian for 'rulers of foreign lands', took power at [[e:avaris|Avaris]] in the eastern Delta and captured [[e:memphis-egypt|Memphis]], ending the [[s:middle-kingdom-of-egypt|Middle Kingdom of Egypt]]. Later Egyptian tradition portrayed this as an invasion, but it grew from a long-settled Canaanite population in the Delta.
fifteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.r: The [[e:hyksos|Hyksos]] adopted pharaonic titles and Egyptian administration while keeping Levantine customs at [[e:avaris|Avaris]], where their great palaces and temples have been excavated. They worshipped [[e:seth|Seth]], identified with the storm god [[e:baal|Baal]], and traded widely with [[e:canaan|Canaan]] and [[e:cyprus|Cyprus]]. Their era spread the horse and [[e:chariot|chariot]] in [[e:egypt|Egypt]], and the [[e:rhind-mathematical-papyrus|Rhind Mathematical Papyrus]] was copied under [[e:apepi|Apepi]]. [[e:khyan|Khyan's]] name appears on objects found as far as [[s:palace-state-of-knossos|Knossos]] and [[e:baghdad|Baghdad]].
fifteenth-dynasty-of-egypt.e: The [[s:seventeenth-dynasty-of-egypt|Seventeenth Dynasty of Egypt]] at [[s:thebes|Thebes]] went to war against [[e:apepi|Apepi]]. [[e:ahmose-i|Ahmose I]], who came to the throne around 1550 BCE, captured [[e:avaris|Avaris]] some years later and then besieged [[e:sharuhen|Sharuhen]] in southern [[e:canaan|Canaan]], driving out the [[e:hyksos|Hyksos]] and founding the [[s:egyptian-empire-new-kingdom|Egyptian Empire New Kingdom]].

free-imperial-city-of-pfullendorf.t: Small Swabian imperial city north of Lake Constance, chartered by Frederick II in 1220 and a modest Catholic member of the Swabian city leagues.
free-imperial-city-of-pfullendorf.o: Pfullendorf was the seat of counts whose lands passed to the [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]] in the later 12th century. In 1220 [[e:frederick-ii|Emperor Frederick II]] granted the town its charter, and it became an imperial city on the roads between the [[e:danube|Danube]] and [[e:lake-constance|Lake Constance]].
free-imperial-city-of-pfullendorf.r: The town was governed by a council with [[e:guild|guild]] participation and lived from linen weaving, crafts and its market for the surrounding countryside. Its small territory included a few villages. It joined the Swabian city leagues and later the Swabian imperial circle, but remained a minor power, and it stayed Catholic during the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]].
free-imperial-city-of-pfullendorf.e: Pfullendorf lost its imperial freedom in 1803 when it was annexed by the [[s:margraviate-of-baden|Margraviate of Baden]], soon the [[s:grand-duchy-of-baden|Grand Duchy of Baden]]. It is now a small town in [[e:baden-wurttemberg|Baden-Württemberg]] with a well-preserved old centre and parts of its medieval walls.

frentani.t: Oscan-speaking people of the central Adriatic coast, related to the Samnites, who became allies of Rome in 304 BCE.
frentani.o: The Frentani occupied the coastal hills of modern [[e:molise|Molise]] and southern [[e:abruzzo|Abruzzo]] between the [[e:sangro|Sangro]] and the [[e:fortore|Fortore]] rivers. Ancient writers considered them of Samnite stock, and they spoke [[e:oscan-language|Oscan]]. Their history before [[e:rome|Rome]] is known only from scattered references.
frentani.r: Their main centres included [[e:vasto|Histonium]] (Vasto), [[e:lanciano|Anxanum]] (Lanciano) and [[e:larino|Larinum]], which some writers treated as a separate people. They farmed, herded and traded along the coast. They usually kept apart from the [[s:samnite-league|Samnite League]] and its wars with [[e:rome|Rome]].
frentani.e: The Frentani made an alliance with [[e:rome|Rome]] in 304 BCE, at the end of the [[e:second-samnite-war|Second Samnite War]], and fought for Rome against [[e:hannibal|Hannibal]]. They joined the Italian rebels in the [[e:social-war-91-87-bce|Social War]] of 91–88 BCE, then received citizenship and were absorbed into Roman [[e:italy|Italy]].

first-portuguese-republic.t: Portugal's first republic, an era of anticlerical reform and chronic instability with some 45 governments in under 16 years.
first-portuguese-republic.o: After the assassination of King Carlos I in 1908, republican sentiment grew in [[e:lisbon|Lisbon]]. On 5 October 1910 a revolt by soldiers, sailors and [[e:carbonaria-portugal|Carbonária]] militants overthrew [[e:manuel-ii-of-portugal|Manuel II]], and a provisional government under [[e:teofilo-braga|Teófilo Braga]] proclaimed the republic, ending the [[s:kingdom-of-portugal|Kingdom of Portugal]].
first-portuguese-republic.r: The Constitution of 1911 created a parliamentary republic. Governments led by [[e:afonso-costa|Afonso Costa]] separated Church and state, expelled the [[e:jesuits|Jesuits]] and legalised divorce. Portugal entered the [[e:first-world-war|First World War]] in 1916 and suffered heavy losses at [[e:battle-of-la-lys-1918|La Lys]] in 1918. Strikes, coups, bombings and [[e:sidonio-pais|Sidónio Pais's]] brief dictatorship of 1917-1918 marked the period, along with the royalist [[s:monarchy-of-the-north|Monarchy of the North]].
first-portuguese-republic.e: On 28 May 1926 a military coup led by General [[e:manuel-gomes-da-costa|Gomes da Costa]] overthrew the republic and set up the [[s:ditadura-nacional|Ditadura Nacional]].

first-mexican-empire.t: The short-lived empire of Agustín de Iturbide, the first independent Mexican state, which briefly stretched from California to Costa Rica.
first-mexican-empire.o: In February 1821 the royalist officer [[e:agustin-de-iturbide|Agustín de Iturbide]] joined the insurgent [[e:vicente-guerrero|Vicente Guerrero]] in the [[e:plan-of-iguala|Plan of Iguala]], promising independence, [[e:catholicism|Catholicism]] and equality under a [[e:constitutional-monarchy|constitutional monarchy]]. The last Spanish [[e:viceroy-of-india|viceroy]], [[e:juan-odonoju|Juan O'Donojú]], accepted it in the [[e:treaty-of-cordoba|Treaty of Córdoba]] in August, and the Army of the Three Guarantees entered [[e:mexico-city|Mexico City]] on 27 September 1821.
first-mexican-empire.r: A regency governed while a European prince was sought, but none accepted, and in May 1822 crowds and soldiers acclaimed [[e:agustin-de-iturbide|Iturbide]] as Emperor Agustín I. [[e:central-america|Central America]] joined the empire in January 1822. Iturbide clashed with the congress over money and power and dissolved it in October 1822. The treasury was empty, the army unpaid and the provinces restless.
first-mexican-empire.e: [[e:antonio-lopez-de-santa-anna|Antonio López de Santa Anna]] rose at [[e:veracruz-city|Veracruz]] in December 1822, and the [[e:plan-of-casa-mata|Plan of Casa Mata]] in 1823 won over the army. [[e:agustin-de-iturbide|Iturbide]] abdicated in March 1823 and went into exile; on his return in 1824 he was executed. [[e:central-america|Central America]] broke away, and [[s:mexico|Mexico]] became the [[s:first-mexican-republic|First Mexican Republic]].

federal-republic-of-central-america.t: Federation of the five former provinces of the Kingdom of Guatemala, a liberal experiment that collapsed in civil war after less than two decades.
federal-republic-of-central-america.o: The provinces of the [[s:captaincy-general-of-guatemala|Captaincy General of Guatemala]] declared independence from [[e:spain|Spain]] in September 1821 and were absorbed into the [[s:first-mexican-empire|First Mexican Empire]] in 1822. After [[e:agustin-de-iturbide|Iturbide]]'s fall, a congress in [[e:guatemala-city|Guatemala City]] declared them independent on 1 July 1823 as the United Provinces of Central America, and a federal constitution followed in 1824.
federal-republic-of-central-america.r: [[s:republic-of-guatemala|Guatemala]], [[s:republic-of-el-salvador|El Salvador]], [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]], [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]] and [[s:republic-of-costa-rica|Costa Rica]] each had their own governments under a weak federal president. Liberals and conservatives, and [[e:guatemala|Guatemala]] and its smaller neighbours, fought a civil war from 1826 to 1829. [[e:francisco-morazan|Francisco Morazán]] won and, as president from 1830, pursued anticlerical reforms, expelled religious orders and moved the capital to [[e:san-salvador|San Salvador]] in 1834. The federation was chronically short of revenue.
federal-republic-of-central-america.e: A rural revolt led by [[e:rafael-carrera|Rafael Carrera]], fuelled by a cholera epidemic and resentment of liberal reforms, broke federal power in [[s:republic-of-guatemala|Guatemala]]. [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]], [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]] and [[s:republic-of-costa-rica|Costa Rica]] seceded in 1838, and [[e:francisco-morazan|Morazán]] was defeated in 1840. The federation dissolved by 1841; Morazán was executed in Costa Rica in 1842.

free-imperial-city-of-donauworth.t: A Swabian imperial city on the Danube whose sectarian riot of 1606 and seizure by Bavaria helped set Europe on the road to the Thirty Years' War.
free-imperial-city-of-donauworth.o: Donauwörth grew where the [[e:wornitz|Wörnitz]] meets the [[e:danube|Danube]], beside the [[e:holy-cross-abbey-donauworth|Holy Cross abbey]] and a castle. A [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]] possession, it later fell under the dukes of [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]], from whom it repeatedly bought back its freedom. It counted as an imperial city from about 1301, although it was pledged to Bavaria again from 1376 until 1434.
free-imperial-city-of-donauworth.r: A council of [[e:burghers|burghers]] governed the town, which prospered from [[e:danube|Danube]] trade and the road between [[s:free-imperial-city-of-nuremberg|Nuremberg]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-augsburg|Augsburg]]. Most citizens became Lutheran, while the Benedictine [[e:holy-cross-abbey-donauworth|Holy Cross abbey]] kept a Catholic minority. In 1606 Protestant townspeople attacked a Catholic procession, and the [[e:aulic-council|Imperial Aulic Council]] placed the city under the imperial ban.
free-imperial-city-of-donauworth.e: [[e:maximilian-i-elector-of-bavaria|Duke Maximilian]] I of [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] executed the ban in 1607, occupied Donauwörth, re-Catholicised it and in 1609 annexed it. Alarmed Protestant princes formed the [[e:protestant-union|Protestant Union]] in 1608, and the [[e:catholic-league|Catholic League]] answered in 1609. Apart from a brief restoration of its imperial freedom from 1705 to 1714, the town has remained Bavarian ever since.

fourth-brazilian-republic.t: Brazil's democratic Populist Republic, the era of Petrobras and Brasília, which ended with the military coup of 1964.
fourth-brazilian-republic.o: After the fall of the [[s:estado-novo-brazil|Estado Novo (Brazil)]] in 1945, General [[e:eurico-gaspar-dutra|Eurico Gaspar Dutra]] was elected president, and a new democratic constitution was adopted in 1946. It restored Congress, parties and elections, though illiterate people could not vote.
fourth-brazilian-republic.r: [[e:getulio-vargas|Getúlio Vargas]] returned as elected president in 1950 and founded [[e:petrobras|Petrobras]], the state oil company, in 1953. Facing a political crisis, he shot himself in 1954. [[e:juscelino-kubitschek|Juscelino Kubitschek]] promised 'fifty years in five' and built the new capital, [[e:brasilia|Brasília]], inaugurated in 1960. [[e:janio-quadros|Jânio Quadros]] resigned within months in 1961, and the military accepted his vice-president [[e:joao-goulart|João Goulart]] only under a temporary parliamentary system.
fourth-brazilian-republic.e: [[e:joao-goulart|Goulart]]'s proposals for land reform and his ties to the left alarmed the military, the middle classes and the [[s:united-states|United States]]. A coup on 31 March and 1 April 1964 deposed him and began the [[s:brazilian-military-dictatorship|Brazilian military dictatorship]].

free-imperial-city-of-muhlhausen.t: Thuringian imperial city famous as the base of Thomas Müntzer during the Peasants' War and for one of the oldest law books written in German.
free-imperial-city-of-muhlhausen.o: [[e:muhlhausen|Mühlhausen]] grew around a royal palace and was favoured by the [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]] emperors, gaining the status of an imperial city by about 1180. Around 1200 to 1230 its law was set down in the [[e:muhlhausen-reichsrechtsbuch|Mühlhausen Reichsrechtsbuch]], one of the earliest legal texts in German.
free-imperial-city-of-muhlhausen.r: A council of patricians and later [[e:guild|guild]] representatives ruled the city, which grew rich from cloth, woad and trade, joined the [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanseatic League]] and allied with [[e:erfurt|Erfurt]] and [[s:free-imperial-city-of-nordhausen|Nordhausen]] in a Thuringian city league. In 1525 the radical preacher [[e:thomas-muntzer|Thomas Müntzer]] made [[e:muhlhausen|Mühlhausen]] his base, set up the Eternal League and led its men to defeat at [[e:battle-of-frankenhausen|Frankenhausen]] in the [[e:german-peasants-war|Peasants' War]].
free-imperial-city-of-muhlhausen.e: After 1525 the city lost its freedom for two decades under [[e:saxons|Saxon]] and Hessian control, regaining imperial status in 1548. It was annexed by [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] in 1802, belonged to the [[s:kingdom-of-westphalia|Kingdom of Westphalia]] from 1807 to 1813, and then returned to Prussia; it is now in [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]].

federation-of-malaya.t: Federation of Malay states and settlements that fought the communist Emergency and won independence from Britain in 1957.
federation-of-malaya.o: The Federation of [[e:malaya|Malaya]] replaced the [[s:malayan-union|Malayan Union]] on 1 February 1948, restoring the [[e:sovereignty|sovereignty]] of the nine Malay rulers and joining their states with [[s:prince-of-wales-island|Penang]] and [[e:malacca|Malacca]] under a British high commissioner. Months later the [[e:malayan-communist-party|Malayan Communist Party]] launched an armed revolt, and the government declared the [[e:malayan-emergency|Malayan Emergency]].
federation-of-malaya.r: Under the [[e:briggs-plan|Briggs Plan]] and High Commissioner [[e:gerald-templer|Gerald Templer]], half a million rural Chinese were moved into new villages to cut off the [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrillas]]. The Alliance of [[e:united-malays-national-organisation|UMNO]], the [[e:malaysian-chinese-association|Malayan Chinese Association]] and the [[e:malaysian-indian-congress|Malayan Indian Congress]] won the 1955 election under [[e:tunku-abdul-rahman|Tunku Abdul Rahman]], who negotiated independence on 31 August 1957. A rotating king, the [[e:yang-di-pertuan-agong|Yang di-Pertuan Agong]], was chosen from the rulers.
federation-of-malaya.e: The Emergency was declared over in 1960, though communist [[e:guerrilla-warfare|guerrillas]] remained on the Thai border. On 16 September 1963 the federation joined with [[s:singapore|Singapore]], [[e:sabah|Sabah]] and [[s:raj-of-sarawak|Sarawak]] to form [[s:malaysia|Malaysia]], which kept its constitution and institutions.

fidach.t: A Pictish province named in the legend of the seven sons of Cruithne, of uncertain location, perhaps around Moray and Ross.
fidach.o: Fidach is known only from medieval lists of the seven Pictish provinces, which named them after legendary sons of [[e:cruithne-legendary-king|Cruithne]], the father of the [[e:picts|Picts]]. Its location is not stated, and historians have suggested [[s:kingdom-of-moray|Moray]], [[e:ross-scotland|Ross]] or the area around the [[e:moray-firth|Moray Firth]].
fidach.r: Nothing is known of its rulers, society or government beyond its inclusion in the province lists. It was presumably one of the regional territories of [[s:kingdom-of-the-picts|Pictland]], subject to the kings of the [[e:picts|Picts]].
fidach.e: Like the other provinces, it disappeared as a distinct unit when [[s:kingdom-of-the-picts|Pictland]] was absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-scotland|Kingdom of Scotland]] in the 9th and 10th centuries.

free-province-of-guayaquil.t: The independent port province of Guayaquil, freed in 1820, whose fate was settled when Bolívar annexed it on the eve of his meeting with San Martín.
free-province-of-guayaquil.o: On 9 October 1820 a group of patriots in [[e:guayaquil|Guayaquil]], the main port of the [[s:royal-audiencia-of-quito|Royal Audiencia of Quito]], overthrew the Spanish authorities. A cabildo declared the Free Province of Guayaquil, with the poet [[e:jose-joaquin-de-olmedo|José Joaquín de Olmedo]] as head of government.
free-province-of-guayaquil.r: The province adopted a provisional regulation of government and created an army, the [[e:protective-division-of-quito|Protective Division of Quito]], to free the highlands. Its first campaigns failed, but with troops sent by [[e:simon-bolivar|Bolívar]] under [[e:antonio-jose-de-sucre|Antonio José de Sucre]], and Peruvian reinforcements, the patriots won at [[e:battle-of-pichincha|Pichincha]] in May 1822. [[e:guayaquil|Guayaquil's]] elite was divided over joining [[s:gran-colombia|Gran Colombia]], [[e:peru|Peru]] or staying independent.
free-province-of-guayaquil.e: [[e:simon-bolivar|Bolívar]] entered [[e:guayaquil|Guayaquil]] in July 1822 and annexed it to [[s:gran-colombia|Gran Colombia]]; [[e:jose-joaquin-de-olmedo|Olmedo]] left in protest. Days later Bolívar met [[e:jose-de-san-martin|San Martín]] in the [[e:guayaquil-conference|Guayaquil Conference]]. Guayaquil became part of the [[s:republic-of-ecuador|Republic of Ecuador]] in 1830.

free-imperial-city-of-turckheim.t: A walled Alsatian wine town, one of the smallest members of the Decapolis, near which Turenne won a decisive battle for France in 1675.
free-imperial-city-of-turckheim.o: Turckheim grew at the entrance to the [[e:fecht|Fecht]] valley near [[s:free-imperial-city-of-colmar|Colmar]], on lands long linked to the abbey of [[s:kingdom-of-munster|Munster]]. Walled in the early 14th century, it was recognised as an imperial city around 1312 and in 1354 joined the [[s:decapolis|Decapolis]], the league of ten Alsatian imperial cities.
free-imperial-city-of-turckheim.r: A council of [[e:burghers|burghers]] ruled the town, whose wealth came almost wholly from its vineyards; its three gates and much of its wall survive. It remained Catholic during the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]]. The round of the night watchman, still re-enacted in summer, recalls the town's tradition of guarding its own walls.
free-imperial-city-of-turckheim.e: After 1648 the [[s:decapolis|Decapolis]] came under French protection. On 5 January 1675 [[e:henri-de-la-tour-d-auvergne-viscount-of-turenne|Marshal Turenne]] defeated the imperial army at the Battle of Turckheim, securing [[e:alsace|Alsace]], and the [[e:treaties-of-nijmegen|Treaty of Nijmegen]] of 1679 confirmed annexation by the [[s:kingdom-of-france|Kingdom of France]]. It is now in the [[e:haut-rhin|Haut-Rhin]] [[e:departement|department]].

france-antarctique.t: A short-lived French colony in Guanabara Bay whose destruction by the Portuguese led directly to the founding of Rio de Janeiro.
france-antarctique.o: In 1555 the French admiral [[e:nicolas-durand-de-villegaignon|Nicolas Durand de Villegaignon]], backed by Admiral [[e:gaspard-de-coligny|Gaspard de Coligny]], sailed to [[e:guanabara-bay|Guanabara Bay]] in [[s:new-republic-brazil|Brazil]] with some 600 settlers. They built [[e:fort-coligny|Fort Coligny]] on a small island and allied with the [[e:tupinamba|Tupinambá]], who traded [[e:brazilwood|brazilwood]] with French merchants.
france-antarctique.r: The colony was intended partly as a refuge for [[e:huguenots|French Protestants]], and a group of [[e:calvinism|Calvinists]] sent from [[s:republic-of-geneva|Geneva]] arrived in 1557, including [[e:jean-de-lery|Jean de Léry]], whose account of the [[e:tupinamba|Tupinambá]] became a classic of travel writing. [[e:nicolas-durand-de-villegaignon|Villegaignon]], however, quarrelled with them over doctrine and expelled them, and some were executed. Harsh discipline and desertions weakened the settlement.
france-antarctique.e: Governor-general [[e:mem-de-sa|Mem de Sá]] destroyed [[e:fort-coligny|Fort Coligny]] in 1560. His nephew [[e:estacio-de-sa|Estácio de Sá]] founded [[e:rio-de-janeiro|Rio de Janeiro]] in 1565 and, with Portuguese and [[e:temimino|Temiminó]] forces, drove the remaining French and their [[e:tupinamba|Tupinambá]] allies from the bay by 1567.

free-cities-of-menton-and-roquebrune.t: Two Riviera towns that broke away from Monaco in 1848 over taxes on their lemons and lived as free cities until France bought them.
free-cities-of-menton-and-roquebrune.o: [[e:menton|Menton]] and [[e:roquebrune-cap-martin|Roquebrune]] formed most of the [[s:principality-of-monaco|Principality of Monaco]]'s territory and income, through their lemon and olive trade. Resentment at Prince [[e:florestan-i-prince-of-monaco|Florestan I]]'s taxes and monopolies boiled over in 1848, and in March the two towns declared themselves [[e:free-imperial-city|free cities]] under the protection of the [[s:kingdom-of-sardinia|Kingdom of Sardinia]].
free-cities-of-menton-and-roquebrune.r: The towns governed themselves through elected councils, with Sardinian troops present. A plebiscite favoured union with [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]], but it was never formally completed because of diplomatic objections. Their economy remained based on citrus fruit, and [[e:menton|Menton]] began to attract winter visitors.
free-cities-of-menton-and-roquebrune.e: After [[e:sardinia|Sardinia]] ceded [[e:nice|Nice]] to [[e:france|France]] in 1860, [[e:menton|Menton]] and [[e:roquebrune-cap-martin|Roquebrune]] voted to join France. In 1861 Prince [[e:charles-iii-prince-of-monaco|Charles III]] of [[s:principality-of-monaco|Monaco]] sold his rights to [[e:napoleon-iii|Napoleon III's]] [[s:second-french-empire|Second French Empire]] for four million francs.

free-imperial-city-of-esslingen.t: Wine town on the Neckar that was a leading Swabian imperial city, founding place of the Swabian League and a lasting rival of Württemberg.
free-imperial-city-of-esslingen.o: [[e:esslingen-am-neckar|Esslingen]] grew around a shrine of Saint Vitalis and a bridge over the [[e:neckar|Neckar]], gaining market rights in the Carolingian period. The [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]] favoured the town, and it was treated as an imperial city by the early 13th century, its privileges confirmed by Frederick II around 1219.
free-imperial-city-of-esslingen.r: A council of patricians and [[e:guild|guilds]] governed the town, which prospered from wine, cloth and bridge tolls. Its position next to Württemberg led to repeated wars with the counts of Württemberg in the 14th and 15th centuries. In 1488 the [[e:swabian-league|Swabian League]] was founded at [[e:esslingen-am-neckar|Esslingen]], and the city hosted the imperial governing council in the 1520s. It adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in 1531.
free-imperial-city-of-esslingen.e: [[e:esslingen-am-neckar|Esslingen]] lost its freedom in 1802 when it was annexed by Württemberg, its old enemy. It became an industrial town known for machine building and remains in [[e:baden-wurttemberg|Baden-Württemberg]], with its Gothic churches and old town hall.

finnish-democratic-republic.t: Soviet puppet government created for Finland at the start of the Winter War, led by Otto Wille Kuusinen and abandoned in 1940.
finnish-democratic-republic.o: On 30 November 1939 the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] invaded [[s:republic-of-finland|Finland]]. The next day it announced the formation of the Finnish Democratic Republic, nominally based in the border town of Terijoki, with the exiled Finnish communist [[e:otto-wille-kuusinen|Otto Wille Kuusinen]] as head. The [[e:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] recognised it as [[e:finland|Finland's]] only legitimate government and signed a treaty of mutual assistance with it.
finnish-democratic-republic.r: The 'Terijoki government' existed mainly on paper and was run from [[e:moscow|Moscow]]. It raised a Finnish People's Army from Soviet [[e:finns|Finns]] and [[s:karelians|Karelians]], intended to enter Helsinki behind the [[e:red-army|Red Army]]. Finns overwhelmingly rejected it, and it helped unite Finnish society behind its real government.
finnish-democratic-republic.e: Finnish resistance forced the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]] to negotiate with the Helsinki government. The [[e:moscow-peace-treaty|Moscow Peace Treaty]] of March 1940 ended the war, and the puppet government was quietly dissolved. Its leaders and territory were merged into the new [[s:karelo-finnish-soviet-socialist-republic|Karelo-Finnish Soviet Socialist Republic]], with [[e:otto-wille-kuusinen|Kuusinen]] as its head.

free-france.t: Charles de Gaulle's government-in-exile and armed forces, which kept France in the war against Germany after 1940 and rallied much of the empire.
free-france.o: On 18 June 1940 General [[e:charles-de-gaulle|Charles de Gaulle]], refusing the armistice, broadcast from [[e:london|London]] on the BBC calling on the French to continue fighting. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] recognised him as leader of the Free French, and in August 1940 [[e:chad|Chad]], under its governor [[e:felix-eboue|Félix Éboué]], joined his cause, followed by most of [[s:french-equatorial-africa|French Equatorial Africa]].
free-france.r: Free [[e:france|France]] built an army and navy, fought at [[e:battle-of-bir-hakeim|Bir Hakeim]] in 1942 and gathered colonies in [[e:africa|Africa]] and the Pacific. A [[e:french-national-committee|French National Committee]] was set up in [[e:london|London]] in 1941. [[e:charles-de-gaulle|De Gaulle's]] envoy [[e:jean-moulin|Jean Moulin]] united the internal Resistance in 1943. That year the movement moved to [[e:algiers|Algiers]] and merged with [[e:henri-giraud|Henri Giraud's]] forces in the [[e:french-committee-of-national-liberation|French Committee of National Liberation]].
free-france.e: In June 1944 the committee became the [[s:provisional-government-of-the-french-republic|Provisional Government of the French Republic]], which returned to [[e:paris|Paris]] after its liberation in August 1944 and restored the Republic.
