frisian-kingdom.t: Pagan kingdom of the North Sea coast, ruler of the trading port of Dorestad, which resisted the Franks for over a century.
frisian-kingdom.o: After the Roman period the coastal [[e:low-countries|Low Countries]] were resettled from the 5th century, and by around 600 the [[s:frisii|Frisians]] held a realm stretching along the coast from the [[e:zwin|Zwin]] to the [[e:weser|Weser]], later called Magna [[e:frisia|Frisia]]. Its first known king, [[e:aldgisl|Aldgisl]], sheltered the English [[e:bishop|bishop]] [[e:wilfrid|Wilfrid]] in 678.
frisian-kingdom.r: The [[s:frisii|Frisians]] were seafaring traders whose merchants carried cloth, slaves and goods across the [[e:north-sea|North Sea]], and their emporium of [[e:dorestad|Dorestad]] on the [[e:rhine|Rhine]] was one of the busiest ports in north-west [[e:europe|Europe]]. Their [[e:silver|silver]] sceattas circulated widely. King [[e:redbad|Redbad]] opposed the Christian mission of [[e:willibrord|Willibrord]].
frisian-kingdom.e: [[e:pippin-of-herstal|Pippin of Herstal]] defeated [[e:redbad|Redbad]] around 690 and took [[e:dorestad|Dorestad]] and [[s:lordship-of-utrecht|Utrecht]], but Redbad recovered much ground before his death in 719. In 734 [[e:charles-martel|Charles Martel]] defeated and killed King [[e:poppo-of-frisia|Poppo]] at the [[e:battle-of-the-boarn|Boarn]], and [[e:frisia|Frisia]] was absorbed into the [[s:kingdom-of-the-franks|Kingdom of the Franks]].

free-imperial-city-of-wangen.t: Small Catholic imperial city in the western Allgäu, a market for linen and scythes that kept its freedom until 1802.
free-imperial-city-of-wangen.o: [[e:wangen-im-allgau|Wangen]] grew around a settlement linked to the [[s:imperial-abbey-of-saint-gall|Imperial Abbey of Saint Gall]], which held rights there from the 9th century. The [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]] developed the town, and after their fall it was recognised as an imperial city by Rudolf I in 1286.
free-imperial-city-of-wangen.r: A council of [[e:burghers|burghers]] ruled the town and its small territory. Linen weaving, scythe making and the market for the western [[e:allgau|Allgäu]] were its main trades. [[e:wangen-im-allgau|Wangen]] remained Catholic during the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] and was a member of the Swabian imperial circle. It suffered heavily in [[e:thirty-tyrants|the Thirty]] Years War.
free-imperial-city-of-wangen.e: [[e:wangen-im-allgau|Wangen]] lost its freedom to [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]] in 1802 and passed to Württemberg in 1810. It is now a town in [[e:baden-wurttemberg|Baden-Württemberg]] with a well-preserved old centre, gate towers and painted houses.

french-florida.t: A short-lived Huguenot colony on the St Johns River whose destruction by Spain in 1565 secured Florida for the Spanish crown.
french-florida.o: Backed by Admiral [[e:gaspard-de-coligny|Gaspard de Coligny]], the Protestant captain [[e:jean-ribault|Jean Ribault]] sailed to [[e:florida|Florida]] in 1562 and left a small garrison at [[e:charlesfort|Charlesfort]], on [[e:parris-island|Parris Island]] in modern [[e:south-carolina|South Carolina]], which was soon abandoned. In 1564 [[e:rene-goulaine-de-laudonniere|René Goulaine de Laudonnière]] brought a second expedition and built Fort Caroline near the mouth of the [[e:st-johns-river|St Johns River]].
french-florida.r: The colony was a fortified outpost of a few hundred soldiers, artisans and [[e:huguenots|Huguenot]] settlers rather than a governed territory. It depended on food from the [[e:timucua|Timucua]] chief [[e:saturiwa|Saturiwa]] and his neighbours, and hunger and mutiny troubled it. The artist [[e:jacques-le-moyne-de-morgues|Jacques Le Moyne de Morgues]] drew the Timucua, leaving some of the earliest European images of [[e:north-america|North America]].
french-florida.e: In 1565 [[e:philip-ii-of-spain|Philip II]] sent [[e:pedro-menendez-de-aviles|Pedro Menéndez de Avilés]], who founded [[e:st-augustine-florida|St Augustine]], captured Fort Caroline and executed [[e:jean-ribault|Ribault]] and his shipwrecked men at [[e:matanzas-inlet|Matanzas Inlet]]. [[e:dominique-de-gourgues|Dominique de Gourgues]] avenged them in 1568, but [[e:france|France]] did not return, leaving [[s:spanish-florida|Spanish Florida]] in control.

first-dominican-republic.t: The first Dominican republic, won from Haiti in 1844 and dominated by the rival strongmen Pedro Santana and Buenaventura Báez until its annexation by Spain.
first-dominican-republic.o: The [[e:secret-society|secret society]] [[e:la-trinitaria|La Trinitaria]], founded in 1838 by [[e:juan-pablo-duarte|Juan Pablo Duarte]], organised resistance to Haitian rule. On 27 February 1844 [[e:francisco-del-rosario-sanchez|Francisco del Rosario Sánchez]] and [[e:ramon-matias-mella|Ramón Matías Mella]] proclaimed independence at the [[e:puerta-del-conde|Puerta del Conde]] in [[e:santo-domingo|Santo Domingo]]. The [[e:cattle|cattle]] rancher [[e:pedro-santana|Pedro Santana]] defeated the Haitian army and soon exiled Duarte and the other founders.
first-dominican-republic.r: The constitution of San Cristóbal of November 1844 included Article 210, giving [[e:pedro-santana|Santana]] dictatorial powers. Santana and [[e:buenaventura-baez|Buenaventura Báez]] alternated in power, each seeking foreign protection from [[e:france|France]], [[e:spain|Spain]] or the [[s:united-states|United States]]. The country repeatedly defended itself against Haitian invasions under [[e:faustin-soulouque|Faustin Soulouque]], notably at [[e:battle-of-las-carreras|Las Carreras]] in 1849 and at [[e:battle-of-santome|Santomé]] and [[e:battle-of-sabana-larga|Sabana Larga]] in 1855 to 1856. Tobacco from the [[e:cibao|Cibao]] valley and mahogany were the main exports; [[e:printing-press|printing]] of [[e:paper-money|paper money]] caused ruinous [[e:inflation|inflation]].
first-dominican-republic.e: Fearing renewed Haitian attack and seeking to keep power, [[e:pedro-santana|Santana]] negotiated the country's annexation to [[e:spain|Spain]], proclaimed on 18 March 1861, creating the [[s:province-of-santo-domingo-1861-1865|Province of Santo Domingo]].

federation-of-central-america-1921-1922.t: Short-lived union of Guatemala, El Salvador and Honduras proclaimed for the centenary of independence in 1921, which fell apart within months.
federation-of-central-america-1921-1922.o: For the hundredth anniversary of independence, delegates of the five Central American states signed a [[e:pact-of-union-1921|Pact of Union]] at [[e:san-jose-costa-rica|San José]] in January 1921. [[s:republic-of-costa-rica|Costa Rica]] did not ratify it and [[s:republic-of-nicaragua|Nicaragua]] withdrew, but [[s:republic-of-guatemala|Guatemala]], [[s:republic-of-el-salvador|El Salvador]] and [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]] went ahead, and a constituent assembly in [[e:tegucigalpa|Tegucigalpa]] adopted a federal constitution in September 1921.
federation-of-central-america-1921-1922.r: The constitution provided for a federal council, congress and courts, with the member states keeping control of most domestic affairs. A provisional federal council met in [[e:tegucigalpa|Tegucigalpa]] while institutions were set up, but the new federation had little money or authority, and member governments were wary of surrendering power.
federation-of-central-america-1921-1922.e: In December 1921 a coup in [[s:republic-of-guatemala|Guatemala]] brought General [[e:jose-maria-orellana|José María Orellana]] to power, and in January 1922 he withdrew [[e:guatemala|Guatemala]] from the federation. [[s:republic-of-el-salvador|El Salvador]] and [[s:republic-of-honduras|Honduras]] followed, and the federation dissolved in early 1922. It was the last formal attempt at Central American political union.

free-state-of-oldenburg.t: North-west German republic that succeeded the grand duchy and in 1932 elected one of the first Nazi state governments.
free-state-of-oldenburg.o: [[e:frederick-augustus-ii-grand-duke-of-oldenburg|Grand Duke Frederick Augustus II]] abdicated in November 1918, and [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] became a free state, with a constitution adopted in 1919. It kept the detached principalities of [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck|Lübeck]] around [[e:eutin|Eutin]] and [[e:birkenfeld|Birkenfeld]] in the [[e:hunsruck|Hunsrück]].
free-state-of-oldenburg.r: [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] was rural, with dairy farming in the marshes and moors and a naval port at [[e:wilhelmshaven|Wilhelmshaven]] nearby. Its Lutheran north and Catholic south around [[e:cloppenburg|Cloppenburg]] and [[e:vechta|Vechta]] differed politically. In 1932 the [[e:nazi-party|Nazis]] won an absolute majority, and [[e:carl-rover|Carl Röver]] formed one of the first Nazi state governments. In 1937 the [[e:greater-hamburg-act|Greater Hamburg Act]] transferred [[s:free-and-hanseatic-city-of-lubeck|Lübeck]] and [[e:birkenfeld|Birkenfeld]] to [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and gave Wilhelmshaven to Oldenburg.
free-state-of-oldenburg.e: Under the [[e:nazism|Nazis]], [[e:carl-rover|Röver]] became Reich governor for [[s:county-of-oldenburg|Oldenburg]] and [[s:free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen|Bremen]]. After 1945 the state lay in the British zone, and in November 1946 it was merged with [[e:hanover|Hanover]], [[e:brunswick|Brunswick]] and [[s:principality-of-schaumburg-lippe|Schaumburg-Lippe]] into the state of [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]]. Oldenburg survives as a historic region and administrative name.

free-imperial-city-of-dinkelsbuhl.t: A walled imperial city on the Wörnitz whose intact medieval fortifications make it one of Germany's best-preserved old towns.
free-imperial-city-of-dinkelsbuhl.o: Dinkelsbühl grew at a crossing of trade routes on the [[e:wornitz|Wörnitz]] and received town rights under the [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]]. After being pledged by the crown to various lords, it secured its status as a free imperial city in 1351, when Charles IV promised that it would not be pledged again.
free-imperial-city-of-dinkelsbuhl.r: In 1387 the [[e:guild|guilds]] won a share of power in the council. Cloth, scythe-making and trade brought prosperity, visible in the late Gothic church of Saint George. The town became mixed in religion, and the [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] made it one of four imperial cities where Catholics and [[e:lutheranism|Lutherans]] shared council offices equally.
free-imperial-city-of-dinkelsbuhl.e: Swedish troops occupied the town in [[e:thirty-tyrants|the Thirty]] Years' War, but it escaped destruction; local tradition says its children persuaded the Swedish colonel to spare it, a story celebrated in the [[e:kinderzeche|Kinderzeche]] festival. In 1802 it passed to [[e:bavaria|Bavaria]], was Prussian from 1804 to 1806 and then returned to Bavaria. Its walls, gates and houses survive almost intact.

frankish-kingdom-of-soissons.t: Merovingian kingdom of Chlothar I, who from his base at Soissons gradually reunited all the Frankish lands.
frankish-kingdom-of-soissons.o: When [[e:clovis-i|Clovis]] died in 511, his youngest son [[e:chlothar-i|Chlothar I]] received the old Frankish heartland in the north, between the Somme and the [[e:scheldt|Scheldt]], ruling from [[e:soissons|Soissons]], the former seat of the [[s:domain-of-soissons|Domain of Soissons]].
frankish-kingdom-of-soissons.r: [[e:chlothar-i|Chlothar]] was the most ruthless of [[e:clovis-i|Clovis]]' sons. In 524 he personally killed two of his young nephews to seize part of the [[s:kingdom-of-orleans|Kingdom of Orléans]]. He shared in the conquest of the [[s:kingdom-of-the-burgundians|Kingdom of the Burgundians]] and of [[e:thuringia|Thuringia]], where he took the princess [[e:radegund|Radegund]] as his wife.
frankish-kingdom-of-soissons.e: Through the deaths of his brothers and nephew, [[e:chlothar-i|Chlothar]] inherited [[s:austrasia|Austrasia]] in 555 and [[e:paris|Paris]] in 558, reuniting the [[s:kingdom-of-the-franks|Kingdom of the Franks]]. He died in 561 and was buried at [[e:abbey-of-saint-medard|Saint-Médard]] in [[e:soissons|Soissons]]. His son [[e:chilperic-i|Chilperic I]] received Soissons, the core of [[s:neustria|Neustria]].

free-city-of-krakow.t: A small city republic around Krakow under the joint protection of Austria, Prussia and Russia, the last free remnant of Poland.
free-city-of-krakow.o: Unable to agree who should have [[e:krakow|Krakow]], the powers at the [[e:congress-of-vienna|Congress of Vienna]] in 1815 made the city and its surrounding district a free, independent and strictly neutral city under the protection of [[e:austria|Austria]], [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and [[e:russia|Russia]].
free-city-of-krakow.r: [[e:krakow|Krakow]] had a senate, an assembly and its own constitution, though the three protecting powers supervised it through their residents. It was the only place where Polish institutions functioned freely, and the [[e:jagiellonian-university|Jagiellonian University]] was a centre of Polish culture. Its free-trade status helped commerce, and it became a refuge for Polish patriots and conspirators.
free-city-of-krakow.e: In February 1846 a national uprising broke out in [[e:krakow|Krakow]] and quickly collapsed. In November 1846 [[e:austria|Austria]] annexed the city with the agreement of [[e:kingdom-of-prussia|Prussia]] and [[e:russia|Russia]], joining it to the [[s:kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria|Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria]] as the Grand [[s:duchy-of-krakow|Duchy of Krakow]].

first-toungoo-empire.t: The largest empire in the history of Southeast Asia, built by Tabinshwehti and Bayinnaung, which briefly ruled from Manipur to Laos and Ayutthaya.
first-toungoo-empire.o: Toungoo, a small Burmese principality on the [[e:sittaung-river|Sittaung]] river, grew in strength under [[e:mingyi-nyo|Mingyi Nyo]], who declared independence from Ava in 1510. His son [[e:tabinshwehti|Tabinshwehti]], from 1530, conquered the [[s:hanthawaddy-kingdom|Hanthawaddy Kingdom]], made [[e:bago|Pegu]] his capital in 1539 and seized [[s:prome-kingdom|Prome]] and much of central [[s:myanmar|Myanmar]].
first-toungoo-empire.r: [[e:bayinnaung|Bayinnaung]], king from 1550, took Ava in 1555, subdued the Shan states and [[s:kingdom-of-manipur|Manipur]], conquered [[s:lan-na|Lan Na]] in 1558 and [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]] in 1564 and 1569, and campaigned in [[s:lan-xang|Lan Xang]]. He governed through [[e:vassal|vassal]] rulers bound by oaths and hostages, standardised weights and law, and patronised [[e:buddhism|Buddhism]]. [[e:bago|Pegu]] was a wealthy port visited by Portuguese and Venetian traders.
first-toungoo-empire.e: After [[e:bayinnaung|Bayinnaung's]] death in 1581 the empire fell apart; [[e:naresuan|Naresuan]] freed [[s:ayutthaya-kingdom|Ayutthaya]] in 1584, and [[e:nanda-bayin|Nanda Bayin's]] wars exhausted the realm. [[e:bago|Pegu]] was sacked by [[s:mrauk-u-kingdom|Arakan]] and Toungoo in 1599. [[e:nyaungyan-min|Nyaungyan Min]] rebuilt the state as the [[s:restored-toungoo-kingdom|Restored Toungoo Kingdom]].

free-imperial-city-of-biberach.t: Upper Swabian imperial city of fustian weavers, shared after 1648 by Catholics and Protestants, where the writer Wieland served as town clerk.
free-imperial-city-of-biberach.o: [[e:biberach-an-der-riss|Biberach]] grew as a market town on the [[e:riss|Riss]] under the [[e:hohenstaufen|Hohenstaufen]], at the crossing of roads in [[e:upper-swabia|Upper Swabia]]. After their fall, it was recognised as an imperial city by Rudolf I around 1282, on the road from Ulm to [[e:lake-constance|Lake Constance]].
free-imperial-city-of-biberach.r: A council of patricians and [[e:guild|guilds]] governed. Fustian weaving and the linen trade made [[e:biberach-an-der-riss|Biberach]] prosperous in the 15th and 16th centuries. The city adopted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]], but after [[e:thirty-tyrants|the Thirty]] Years War it became a parity city in which Catholics and [[e:lutheranism|Lutherans]] shared every office and even the parish church. [[e:christoph-martin-wieland|Christoph Martin Wieland]], born nearby, served as its town clerk from 1760 to 1769.
free-imperial-city-of-biberach.e: [[e:biberach-an-der-riss|Biberach]] lost its freedom in 1802 to [[e:baden|Baden]] and was transferred to Württemberg in 1806. It is now a town in [[e:baden-wurttemberg|Baden-Württemberg]], where a museum and an annual festival recall its parity tradition and [[e:christoph-martin-wieland|Wieland]].

free-imperial-city-of-landau.t: A Palatinate wine town that held imperial-city status for four centuries before Louis XIV annexed it and made it a fortress.
free-imperial-city-of-landau.o: Founded by the counts of [[s:principality-of-leiningen|Leiningen]] around 1260, [[e:landau|Landau]] received town rights from [[e:rudolf-i-of-germany|King Rudolf I]] in 1274, and in 1291 King Rudolf I granted it the privileges of a free imperial city. In the 1320s [[e:louis-iv-holy-roman-emperor|Louis the Bavarian]] pledged the town to the [[e:bishop|bishops]] of [[s:free-imperial-city-of-speyer|Speyer]], and Landau had to buy back its freedom, which it achieved only in 1511.
free-imperial-city-of-landau.r: A walled market town in the vineyards of the southern [[s:electoral-palatinate|Palatinate]], [[e:landau|Landau]] was governed by a council and lived from wine, crafts and trade. From 1521 it belonged to the [[s:decapolis|Decapolis]], the league of Alsatian imperial cities, and it accepted the [[e:protestant-reformation|Reformation]] in the 16th century. Its position made it a target in every war along the upper [[e:rhine|Rhine]].
free-imperial-city-of-landau.e: The [[e:peace-of-westphalia|Peace of Westphalia]] in 1648 placed the [[s:decapolis|Decapolis]] under French protection, and in 1680 [[e:louis-xiv|Louis XIV's]] [[e:reunions|Chambers of Reunion]] annexed [[e:landau|Landau]] outright; Vauban rebuilt it as a great fortress. It passed to the [[s:kingdom-of-bavaria|Kingdom of Bavaria]] in 1816 and is now Landau in der Pfalz in [[e:germany|Germany]].

first-east-turkestan-republic.t: A short-lived Islamic republic proclaimed at Kashgar in 1933 during the rebellions in Xinjiang, the first attempt at an independent Uyghur state.
first-east-turkestan-republic.o: The abolition of the [[s:kumul-khanate|Kumul Khanate]] in 1930 provoked revolts across [[e:xinjiang|Xinjiang]] against Governor [[e:jin-shuren|Jin Shuren]]. In the south, rebels from [[s:kingdom-of-khotan|Khotan]] led by [[e:muhammad-amin-bughra|Muhammad Amin Bughra]] and the cleric [[e:sabit-damulla|Sabit Damulla]] took [[s:kingdom-of-shule|Kashgar]], and on 12 November 1933 proclaimed the Turkish Islamic Republic of East Turkestan.
first-east-turkestan-republic.r: The republic was based on Islamic law and Turkic nationalism, with [[e:sabit-damulla|Sabit Damulla]] as prime minister and the [[e:hami|Kumul]] rebel leader [[e:khoja-niyaz|Khoja Niyaz]] named president, though he never ruled from [[s:kingdom-of-shule|Kashgar]]. It had a constitution, flag and coins but little control beyond the southern oases, and it failed to win recognition from the [[s:soviet-union|Soviet Union]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] or [[s:islamic-emirate-of-afghanistan-2021-present|Afghanistan]].
first-east-turkestan-republic.e: In early 1934 Hui Muslim troops of [[e:ma-zhongying|Ma Zhongying]], retreating from the north, took [[s:kingdom-of-shule|Kashgar]] and crushed the republic. [[e:khoja-niyaz|Khoja Niyaz]] came to terms with the new governor [[e:sheng-shicai|Sheng Shicai]] and handed [[e:sabit-damulla|Sabit Damulla]] over. The idea revived in the [[s:second-east-turkestan-republic|Second East Turkestan Republic]].

free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen.t: Weser port and Hanseatic city that won self-government in the Middle Ages and survives today as Germany's smallest federal state.
free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen.o: [[e:bremen|Bremen]] grew as the seat of the archbishops of [[e:archbishopric-of-hamburg-bremen|Hamburg-Bremen]]. In 1186 [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa]] granted its citizens rights that freed them from many of the archbishop's claims. Joining the [[s:hanseatic-league|Hanseatic League]] in the 13th century, the city slowly won self-government from the [[s:prince-archbishopric-of-bremen|Prince-Archbishopric of Bremen]], symbolised by the [[e:bremen-roland|Roland statue]] of 1404.
free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen.r: A council of merchant families governed from the Gothic town hall, and wealth came from the [[e:weser|Weser]] trade in grain, beer, [[e:timber|timber]] and later tobacco and [[e:coffee-economy|coffee]]. [[e:bremen|Bremen]] adopted the [[e:calvinism|Reformed Protestant]] faith in the late 16th century. Its status as a free imperial city was confirmed by the [[e:linz-diploma|Linz Diploma]] of 1646, protecting it against Swedish claims after 1648.
free-hanseatic-city-of-bremen.e: [[e:bremen|Bremen]] kept its freedom in 1803, was annexed by [[e:first-french-empire|Napoleonic France]] from 1810 to 1813, and joined the [[s:german-confederation|German Confederation]] and [[s:german-empire|German Empire]] as a city-state. Mayor [[e:johann-smidt|Johann Smidt]] founded [[e:bremerhaven|Bremerhaven]] in 1827. Since 1949 the Free Hanseatic City of Bremen has been a federal state of [[e:germany|Germany]].

french-polynesia.t: France's Pacific overseas collectivity of 118 islands around Tahiti, shaped by three decades of nuclear testing and a long debate over autonomy and independence.
french-polynesia.o: In 1946 the [[s:french-establishments-in-oceania|French Establishments in Oceania]] became an overseas territory of the [[s:french-fourth-republic|French Union]], and in 1957 it was renamed French [[e:polynesia|Polynesia]]. The nationalist leader [[e:pouvanaa-a-oopa|Pouvanaa a Oopa]], who campaigned for independence, was arrested in 1958 and exiled after a disputed conviction.
french-polynesia.r: From 1966 to 1996 [[e:france|France]] carried out 193 nuclear tests at [[e:moruroa|Moruroa]] and [[e:fangataufa|Fangataufa]] atolls, first in the atmosphere and later underground, bringing money and jobs but lasting health and environmental harm. The resumption of testing in 1995 caused riots in [[e:papeete|Papeete]]. Statutes of 1984, 1996 and 2004 extended autonomy, and politics was long a contest between [[e:gaston-flosse|Gaston Flosse]], favouring ties to France, and the pro-independence [[e:oscar-temaru|Oscar Temaru]].
french-polynesia.e: French [[e:polynesia|Polynesia]] is an overseas collectivity with its own president and assembly. The [[e:united-nations|United Nations]] relisted it as a non-self-governing territory in 2013. Tourism and black pearls are the main earners alongside French [[e:subsidy|subsidies]].

french-protectorate-in-morocco.t: French rule over most of Morocco from 1912, shaped by Lyautey's modern cities and ended by a nationalist movement led by the sultan himself.
french-protectorate-in-morocco.o: After the [[e:agadir-crisis|Agadir crisis]], [[e:france|France]] forced [[e:sultan|Sultan]] [[e:abd-al-hafid-of-morocco|Abd al-Hafid]] of the [[s:alaouite-sultanate|Alaouite Sultanate]] to sign the [[e:treaty-of-fez|Treaty of Fez]] in March 1912, establishing a [[e:protectorate|protectorate]]. [[e:hubert-lyautey|Hubert Lyautey]], the first resident-general, made [[e:rabat|Rabat]] the capital and spent years subduing the [[e:atlas-mountains|Atlas]] tribes.
french-protectorate-in-morocco.r: The sultan and makhzen remained in place, but the resident-general governed. [[e:hubert-lyautey|Lyautey]] built new European cities beside the old medinas and developed [[e:casablanca|Casablanca's]] port. French settlers took fertile land, and phosphate mining grew. The [[e:berber-dahir|Berber Dahir]] of 1930 sparked nationalist protest, and the [[e:istiqlal-party|Istiqlal]] party demanded independence in 1944.
french-protectorate-in-morocco.e: [[e:france|France]] deposed and exiled [[e:mohammed-v-of-morocco|Sultan Mohammed]] V in 1953, provoking violent unrest. He returned in 1955, and France recognised Moroccan independence in March 1956. Mohammed V adopted the title of king, forming the [[s:kingdom-of-morocco|Kingdom of Morocco]].

free-state-of-lippe.t: Small Westphalian republic whose January 1933 election the Nazis used as a showcase just before Hitler came to power.
free-state-of-lippe.o: [[e:leopold-iv-prince-of-lippe|Prince Leopold IV]] abdicated on 12 November 1918, and Lippe became a free state with [[e:detmold|Detmold]] as capital. A constitution adopted in 1920 established a parliamentary government with a small Landtag.
free-state-of-lippe.r: Lippe was rural, with small farms, furniture making and a tradition of seasonal brickmakers. Social Democrats and liberals generally governed. In the Landtag election of 15 January 1933 the [[e:nazism|Nazis]] concentrated their campaign on the tiny state, with [[e:adolf-hitler|Hitler]] speaking repeatedly, and their gain of votes was presented as proof of momentum two weeks before he became chancellor. Under the [[e:nazi-party|Nazis]] Lippe shared a Reich governor with [[s:principality-of-schaumburg-lippe|Schaumburg-Lippe]], [[e:alfred-meyer|Alfred Meyer]].
free-state-of-lippe.e: After 1945 Lippe was in the British zone. Rather than joining [[e:lower-saxony|Lower Saxony]], it opted in January 1947 to join [[e:north-rhine-westphalia|North Rhine-Westphalia]], under guarantees known as the [[e:lippe-punctations|Lippe Punctations]].

falkland-islands.t: A British territory in the South Atlantic, settled by sheep farmers and claimed by Argentina as the Malvinas, which went to war over it in 1982.
falkland-islands.o: [[e:france|France]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] and [[e:spain|Spain]] had established rival settlements in the islands in the 18th century. In the 1820s the [[s:united-provinces-of-the-rio-de-la-plata|United Provinces of the Río de la Plata]] appointed [[e:luis-vernet|Louis Vernet]] as governor. In January 1833 a British warship expelled the Argentine garrison, and [[e:britain|Britain]] took control. A crown colony was formed in 1841, and [[e:stanley-falkland-islands|Stanley]] became the capital in 1845.
falkland-islands.r: The islands developed as a sheep-farming colony, much of it owned by the [[e:falkland-islands-company|Falkland Islands Company]], with a small population of British descent. [[e:stanley-falkland-islands|Port Stanley]] served ships rounding [[e:cape-horn|Cape Horn]]. [[s:argentine-republic|Argentina]] maintained its claim. On 2 April 1982 [[e:argentina|Argentina's]] military government invaded; a British task force retook the islands, and Argentina surrendered on 14 June after a war that killed over 900 people.
falkland-islands.e: Fishing licences from 1987 transformed the economy. In a 2013 referendum over 99 per cent of voters chose to stay British. The islands remain a [[e:british-overseas-territories|British Overseas Territory]], and [[s:argentine-republic|Argentina]] still claims them.

federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south.t: The British-sponsored union of protected states in the Aden hinterland, created in 1959 to secure Britain's base at Aden.
federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south.o: Facing Arab nationalism and claims by the [[s:mutawakkilite-kingdom-of-yemen|Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen]], [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] encouraged the rulers of the [[s:aden-protectorate|Western Aden Protectorate]] to federate. On 11 February 1959 six states, the [[s:audhali-sultanate|Audhali Sultanate]], [[s:emirate-of-beihan|Emirate of Beihan]], [[s:emirate-of-dhala|Emirate of Dhala]], [[s:fadhli-sultanate|Fadhli Sultanate]], [[s:lower-yafa-sultanate|Lower Yafa Sultanate]] and [[s:upper-aulaqi-sheikhdom|Upper Aulaqi Sheikhdom]], signed the federation treaty with [[e:britain|Britain]].
federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south.r: The federation had a supreme council of rulers and a federal government at [[e:madinat-ash-shab|Al Ittihad]], a new capital built near [[e:aden|Aden]]. [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] kept responsibility for defence and foreign affairs and provided aid and the Federal Regular Army. Other states, including the [[s:sultanate-of-lahej|Sultanate of Lahej]], joined in the following years.
federation-of-arab-emirates-of-the-south.e: In April 1962 the federation was renamed the [[s:federation-of-south-arabia|Federation of South Arabia]], in preparation for the entry of the [[s:colony-of-aden|Colony of Aden]] in 1963.

federal-state-of-the-visayas.t: Revolutionary government of the central Philippines, based in Iloilo, which took over from Spain at the end of 1898.
federal-state-of-the-visayas.o: As the revolution spread to the Visayan islands in 1898, local leaders in Panay organised a cantonal government in [[e:iloilo-city|Iloilo]], inspired by federalist ideas. Revolutionary forces under General [[e:martin-delgado|Martin Delgado]] besieged Iloilo, and on 25 December 1898 the Spanish garrison surrendered, leaving the Federal State of the [[e:visayas|Visayas]] in control.
federal-state-of-the-visayas.r: The federal state was headed by [[e:roque-lopez|Roque Lopez]] as president, with a council representing islands such as Panay and [[e:negros|Negros]], and it acknowledged the authority of [[e:emilio-aguinaldo|Emilio Aguinaldo]]. Its leaders came from the wealthy [[e:sugar-plantation|sugar]]-producing and merchant families of [[e:iloilo-city|Iloilo]]. It lasted only weeks as an effective government.
federal-state-of-the-visayas.e: American troops took [[e:iloilo-city|Iloilo]] on 11 February 1899 at the start of the [[e:philippine-american-war|Philippine-American War]]. The federal government was merged into the [[s:first-philippine-republic|First Philippine Republic]], and resistance on Panay continued until 1901.

french-algeria.t: France's largest settler colony, conquered from 1830 and governed as part of France, whose end in 1962 came after one of the bloodiest wars of decolonisation.
french-algeria.o: [[e:france|France]] invaded the [[s:regency-of-algiers|Regency of Algiers]] in 1830 after a diplomatic incident. Conquest of the interior took decades of brutal war, notably against the [[s:emirate-of-abdelkader|Emirate of Abdelkader]], worn down by [[e:thomas-robert-bugeaud|Thomas-Robert Bugeaud's]] campaigns until its surrender in 1847, and against [[e:kabylia|Kabylia]] and the 1871 [[s:kingdom-of-ait-abbas|Mokrani]] revolt.
french-algeria.r: In 1848 northern [[e:algeria|Algeria]] was divided into French [[e:departement|departments]]. European settlers, later called [[e:pieds-noirs|pieds-noirs]], received land seized from Algerians and held political power, while Muslims were subjects under the Code de l'[[e:indigenat|indigénat]] without full citizenship. The [[e:cremieux-decree|Crémieux Decree]] of 1870 granted citizenship to Algerian [[e:jews|Jews]]. Wine, grain and citrus were key exports.
french-algeria.e: The [[e:setif-and-guelma-massacre|Sétif massacres]] of 1945 hardened nationalism, and the [[e:national-liberation-front-algeria|FLN]] launched the war of independence in 1954. After hundreds of thousands of deaths, the [[e:evian-accords|Évian Accords]] of 1962 under [[e:charles-de-gaulle|de Gaulle]] led to independence that July, and most settlers left for [[e:france|France]].

free-imperial-city-of-worms.t: Ancient Rhine city of the Nibelungenlied, the Concordat of 1122 and Luther's defiance at the Diet of 1521, home of one of Europe's oldest Jewish communities.
free-imperial-city-of-worms.o: Worms was a Roman and Frankish centre, seat of a [[e:bishop|bishop]] and in legend of the Burgundian kings of the [[e:nibelungenlied|Nibelungenlied]]. Its citizens won growing privileges from the Salian emperors, who signed the [[e:concordat-of-worms|Concordat of Worms]] there in 1122. [[e:frederick-barbarossa|Frederick Barbarossa's]] charter of 1184 confirmed the city's freedoms, and it gradually threw off the bishop's lordship.
free-imperial-city-of-worms.r: A council of [[e:burghers|burghers]] ruled, frequently in conflict with the [[e:bishop|bishop]]. Worms hosted many [[e:imperial-diet|imperial diets]], most famously in 1521, when [[e:martin-luther|Martin Luther]] refused to recant before [[e:charles-v-holy-roman-emperor|Charles V]]. Its Jewish community, with [[s:free-imperial-city-of-speyer|Speyer]] and [[e:mainz|Mainz]] one of the [[e:schum-cities|SchUM]] centres of [[e:ashkenazi-jews|Ashkenazi]] learning, had a synagogue and cemetery dating from the 11th century. The city adopted [[e:lutheranism|Lutheranism]].
free-imperial-city-of-worms.e: French troops burned Worms in 1689, and it never fully recovered. [[e:french-first-republic|Revolutionary France]] annexed it in 1797. In 1816 it passed to the [[s:grand-duchy-of-hesse|Grand Duchy of Hesse]], and it is now in [[e:rhineland-palatinate|Rhineland-Palatinate]], where the [[e:schum-cities|SchUM]] sites are a [[e:unesco-world-heritage-site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland.t: A British-created union of Southern Rhodesia, Northern Rhodesia and Nyasaland, rejected by African nationalists and dissolved after ten years.
federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland.o: White settler leaders, chiefly [[e:godfrey-huggins|Godfrey Huggins]] of [[s:southern-rhodesia|Southern Rhodesia]] and [[e:roy-welensky|Roy Welensky]] of [[s:northern-rhodesia|Northern Rhodesia]], pressed for a union of the three British territories in central [[e:africa|Africa]]. Despite African opposition, [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] created the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, or Central African Federation, in 1953, with its capital at [[e:harare|Salisbury]].
federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland.r: A federal government handled defence, economy and railways, while the territories kept their own governments. The federation promised racial 'partnership', but voting rights remained mostly white. [[e:copper|Copper]] revenues financed growth and the [[e:kariba-dam|Kariba Dam]] on the [[e:zambezi|Zambezi]], mainly benefiting [[s:southern-rhodesia|Southern Rhodesia]]. The 1959 emergency in [[s:nyasaland|Nyasaland]] and the [[e:devlin-report|Devlin]] and [[e:monckton-commission|Monckton]] reports undermined its legitimacy.
federation-of-rhodesia-and-nyasaland.e: [[s:united-kingdom|Britain]] allowed [[s:nyasaland|Nyasaland]] and [[s:northern-rhodesia|Northern Rhodesia]] to leave, and the federation was dissolved on 31 December 1963. [[e:malawi|Malawi]] and [[e:zambia|Zambia]] became independent in 1964, while [[s:southern-rhodesia|Southern Rhodesia]] moved towards unilateral independence.
